## Problem
When the Control UI skills page loads with route data, ClawHub security verdicts are never fetched because `ensureInitialData()` short-circuits early after finding agentsList/report in route data. Verdict labels stay stuck as "Unavailable" until manual refresh.

## Fix
Three targeted changes:

1. **`ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`** — Export `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` and `reportHasLinkedClawHubSkills` so the page can call them directly.

2. **`ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`** — In `ensureInitialData()`, after the route-data early return, hydrate verdicts when the report has linked ClawHub skills, verdicts are empty, and no fetch is in progress.

3. **`ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`** — Update `verdictLabel()`, `verdictChipClass()`, and `verdictStatusKind()` to accept an optional `loading` parameter. When verdicts are null but loading is true, show "Pending" (muted style) instead of "Unavailable" (warn), avoiding a flash of misleading state before the fetch completes.

## Testing
- Open Control UI → Skills page
- Verify verdicts populate on first load (no manual refresh needed)
- Disconnect/reconnect: verdicts should show "Pending" while loading, then resolve to actual status
- No change to verdict display when already loaded

Fixes #108647

All navigation funnels through the top-left hamburger — the hardest reach on a phone — so chat-first mobile users pay a two-tap drawer trip for every destination. The chat header exposes four unlabeled icon buttons with no touch tooltips, the command palette opens as a centered desktop box whose lower half the software keyboard covers (with keyboard-only hint copy on a touch screen), thread keys in the sessions table head-ellipsize into identical "agent:main:m…" stubs, and several composer/table controls are below-standard touch targets. ## Why This Change Was Made Presentation-only re-shaping of existing capability for touch; no behavior, route, or data changes. The chat pane header on merged mobile chrome collapses its three secondary actions (thread changes / background tasks / thread files) into one labeled "•••" menu built from the same action descriptors the inline desktop icons consume, so both render paths share one source of truth. target.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in Discord API response bodies
target.body:
## Summary

Reject malformed UTF-8 bytes in Discord API response bodies with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so invalid bytes throw immediately instead of silently becoming U+FFFD in a payload that then passes `JSON.parse`.

## What Problem This Solves

`fetchDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/api.ts:222` downloads Discord API JSON responses and decodes them with a forgiving `TextDecoder` (default `fatal: false`), so invalid bytes are silently replaced with U+FFFD. The corrupted text then passes `JSON.parse` and enters the Discord plugin with mangled field values.

## Root Cause

- Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing.
- Schema validation operates on the already-decoded string, so it cannot detect byte-level corruption after U+FFFD substitution.
- Invariant violated: "HTTP response bytes from Discord API are always valid UTF-8" — not guaranteed for bytes served through a CDN edge or proxy.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to the TextDecoder so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw a `TypeError` before `JSON.parse`. The existing `catch` block already handles `JSON.parse` errors by throwing a `DiscordApiError` with "malformed JSON", and the `TypeError` from TextDecoder also propagates to the same caller error handling.

## User Impact

- **Before**: corrupted Discord API responses are silently accepted with U+FFFD substitution, producing usernames like "test<0xFF>user" in parsed results.
- **After**: corrupted responses are rejected at decode time, surfacing the encoding error immediately.

## Evidence

Proof serves a Discord API JSON response with a raw `0xFF` byte injected inside a string value. Reads it with the exact `readResponseWithLimit` + `TextDecoder.decode()` pattern used by the codebase.

### Before (on main)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-discord-api.mjs
[1] DISCORD API (before) — accepted, username: "test<0xFF>user"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD
Results: 0 passed, 1 failed
```

### After (with fix)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-discord-api.mjs
[2] DISCORD API (after) — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted Discord API response rejected before JSON.parse
Results: 1 passed, 0 failed
PASS: corrupted Discord API response rejected with fatal decoder
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts` — **18 passed, 0 failed**
- `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file
- Existing regression coverage unaffected; no new tests needed (TypeScript layer guarantees `fatal: true` is a compile-time constant on the constructor opts — the behavior change is in the runtime `TextDecoder` built-in)

target.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #93069.

This keeps the config contract honest without stranding existing configs:

- `diagnostics.otel.protocol` now documents and validates the only implemented transport: `http/protobuf`.
- Existing shipped configs with `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` are now handled by `openclaw doctor --fix` instead of simply becoming invalid on upgrade.
- If the old config also had telemetry enabled, doctor disables `diagnostics.otel.enabled` while removing `protocol`, preserving the old runtime behavior where `grpc` never exported telemetry.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` remains a fail-closed runtime override path, and now has focused regression coverage.
- Real gRPC exporter support is intentionally out of scope here.

## Linked context

Closes #93069.

Related review concern: ClawSweeper flagged the first version because it rejected a shipped config value without an upgrade path. This revision adds that doctor migration path and proof.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs no longer get stranded by the stricter schema; doctor removes the unsupported protocol and disables enabled telemetry until the operator chooses an OTLP/HTTP collector.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, Node v25.6.1, branch head `074f6a0b45`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
  const { validateConfigObjectRaw } = await import("./src/config/validation.ts");
  const { migrateLegacyConfig } = await import("./src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.ts");
  const input = { diagnostics: { otel: { enabled: true, endpoint: "http://otel-collector:4317", protocol: "grpc" } } };
  const before = validateConfigObjectRaw(input);
  const migrated = migrateLegacyConfig(input);
  const after = validateConfigObjectRaw(migrated.config ?? {});
  console.log("before.ok=" + before.ok);
  if (!before.ok) console.log("before.issue=" + before.issues.find((issue) => issue.path === "diagnostics.otel.protocol")?.message);
  console.log("migration.changes=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.changes));
  console.log("after.config=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.config?.diagnostics?.otel));
  console.log("after.ok=" + after.ok);
'
```

- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text
before.ok=false
before.issue=Invalid input: expected "http/protobuf" (allowed: "http/protobuf")
migration.changes=["Removed unsupported diagnostics.otel.protocol \"grpc\"; use \"http/protobuf\" with an OTLP/HTTP collector.","Disabled diagnostics.otel.enabled because legacy grpc configs never exported telemetry; re-enable it after choosing an OTLP/HTTP collector."]
after.config={"enabled":false,"endpoint":"http://otel-collector:4317"}
after.ok=true
```

- Observed result after fix: The unsupported `grpc` config is rejected by validation before migration, doctor migration removes `protocol`, disables enabled telemetry, keeps the endpoint intact, and the migrated config validates successfully.
- What was not tested: A live OTLP collector or real telemetry export; real gRPC exporter support is not implemented by this PR.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The direct proof imports the actual config validation and doctor migration modules from the source checkout. The runtime env override path is covered by the focused diagnostics-otel service test below rather than by a live collector run.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): ClawSweeper’s earlier review reproduced the issue by source inspection and flagged the lack of a doctor/migration path for shipped `grpc` configs.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/deprecation-compat.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test-utils.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`
  - Passed: 5 Vitest shards, 343 tests.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

Regression coverage added:

- Doctor migration removes `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` and disables enabled telemetry.
- Doctor preflight reports shipped `grpc` configs as repairable legacy config.
- Doctor config flow applies the repair end to end.
- Config validation reports the allowed value as `http/protobuf`.
- Diagnostics OTel service rejects `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` before exporter startup.
- Deprecation compatibility inventory tracks the migration so it is not deleted accidentally.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes` — unsupported `grpc` config now fails validation, with doctor repair for existing configs.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `Yes` — schema narrows to `http/protobuf`, and doctor migrates legacy `grpc` configs.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No`.

Highest-risk area: upgrade behavior for existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs. The doctor migration is intentionally conservative: it preserves the old no-export outcome by disabling telemetry when the unsupported `grpc` config had been enabled.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of Exa web search could receive silently corrupted titles, highlights, summaries, or extracted text when an upstream response contained malformed UTF-8. The response decoder previously replaced invalid bytes with U+FFFD, allowing the surrounding JSON to parse and the altered content to be presented to the model as genuine search output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exa success responses now reuse the canonical `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http` JSON response reader, which owns bounded body reads, fatal UTF-8 decoding, and JSON parsing for provider integrations. Invalid bytes follow its standard `Exa API: malformed JSON response` error path; response cleanup, result normalization, caching, endpoint policy, and valid UTF-8 behavior are unchanged. No Exa-local parsing strategy or compatibility layer was added.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and the validation results.

## User Impact

Users now receive a deterministic provider error instead of search content containing silent replacement characters when an Exa response is not valid UTF-8. Valid Exa search responses continue to parse normally.

## Evidence

- Runtime dependency probe with the supported Node `TextDecoder` contract:


target.title: fix(web-search): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Web search runtime config lookup paths use `"provider" in <searchObj>` to check whether a provider field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry.

This is the **pre-Zod validation boundary** — the raw POJO config object from `JSON.parse()` before schema validation. These `in` checks operate on the raw object where prototype-chain properties from a crafted `__proto__` survive until the `Object.hasOwn()` gate.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across web search config lookup paths.

### Evidence


**Unit tests**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts` — 32 tests passed (includes 2 own-property tests)

**Runtime proof** (imported real module, tested all 4 `Object.hasOwn` code paths):

```
-- 1/5.  Core semantic proof --
  'provider' in Object.create({ provider: "brave" }):    true
  Object.hasOwn(Object.create({ provider: "brave" })):   false
  -> Object.hasOwn() rejects proto, accepts own

-- 2/5.  Loading real OpenClaw web-search module --
  Module loaded successfully

-- 3/5.  Proto-inherited provider (empty providers list) --
  resolveWebSearchProviderId(proto, []):      ""
  -> Proto-inherited provider REJECTED

-- 4/5.  Own provider selection --
  resolveWebSearchProviderId(own, [fc]):      "firecrawl"
  -> Own provider correctly SELECTED

-- 5/5.  Full tool execution --
  createTool returned:                        OK
  execute() returned:                         {"results":[{"title":"OpenClaw AI","url":"https://openclaw.ai"}]}
  -> Provider tool created and executed SUCCESSFULLY

-- CONTRACT VERIFICATION --
  in operator:         ALL proto fields detected -> WOULD OVERRIDE
  Object.hasOwn():     ALL proto fields ignored -> SAFE
  Own properties:      correctly selected -> BACKWARD COMPAT
  Execution:           firecrawl provider tool executed -> FULL FLOW OK
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading local or paired-node Pi session transcripts through the ACPX plugin could still read an oversized session file into memory when the JSONL file grew after the 32 MiB size preflight.

target.title: fix(session-write-lock): continue watchdog loop past per-lock release errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the session write-lock watchdog aborts its cleanup loop when a single lock's `forceRelease()` throws a filesystem error (e.g. EACCES, EPERM, EISDIR, or a transient I/O fault). On unfixed main, the `await held.forceRelease()` call inside `runLockWatchdogCheck` has no per-iteration error isolation — any exception propagates out of the function, is swallowed by the `.catch(() => {})` in the `setInterval` callback, and **all subsequent stale locks in the same watchdog cycle are left unreleased**.

The watchdog is the only automatic recovery path for session write-locks held past `maxHoldMs`. Stale locks accumulate and block every concurrent session writer with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, preventing agent turns from starting or continuing. Under filesystem instability (disk pressure, NFS mount issues, permission drift), a single failing release can cascade into indefinite lock starvation across all concurrent sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix wraps each `await held.forceRelease()` iteration in its own try/catch block. A failed release is reported to stderr (matching the existing watchdog diagnostic convention) and the loop continues to the next held lock. No other code paths or behavioral contracts change — the watchdog still returns the count of successfully released locks, and `setInterval`/cleanup logic is unchanged.

This follows the principle of best-effort cleanup: one stuck or broken lock must never prevent cleanup of unrelated locks.

## User Impact

- Multi-session and concurrent agent deployments are protected from cascading lock starvation caused by a single filesystem error during watchdog cleanup.
- Operators gain observability: the watchdog now emits `[session-write-lock] failed to release lock <path>: <error>` to stderr when a per-lock release fails.

## Evidence

### Regression test with injected failure

The test "releases the second stale lock when the first force-release throws" in `session-write-lock.test.ts`:

1. Acquires two independent session write-locks with `maxHoldMs: 1` (both immediately stale)
2. Replaces the first lock's file with a directory — this causes `readSidecarLockSnapshot` to fail with EISDIR (not ENOENT) when `forceRelease` tries to clean up, which is the only non-ENOENT path that triggers a throw from the `@openclaw/fs-safe` internals
3. Runs `runLockWatchdogCheck` at a far-future timestamp
4. Asserts `released === 1` — lock A's release threw (caught + logged), lock B was still released
5. Asserts lock B's file is gone (successfully cleaned up)
6. Asserts the EISDIR error was reported to stderr

**On unfixed main**: the EISDIR error propagates out of the loop, `released === 0`, and lock B is never touched. **This test fails on main.**

### Test results

```
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts (52 tests)
   ✓ releases the second stale lock when the first force-release throws
   ✓ watchdog releases stale in-process locks
   ... (50 more passing; 2 pre-existing Windows-only EPERM failures in events.test.ts)
```

### Sibling-surface audit

- `runLockWatchdogCheck` is the only watchdog loop that iterates held entries and calls `forceRelease()`. It is exclusively consumed by `startWatchdogTimer()`.
- `releaseAllLocksSync` uses `SESSION_LOCKS.reset()` (synchronous) — not affected.
- `cleanStaleLockFiles` operates on filesystem-level stale lock scanning, not in-process held entries — not affected.
- The underlying `@openclaw/fs-safe` `releaseHeldLock` wraps internal cleanup in try/catch but re-throws cleanup failures; our fix adds the missing isolation at the watchdog call site.

### Format

`pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passes on both changed files.

target.title: feat(hooks): emit session:aborted + opt-in auto-continue hook
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the stuck-session watchdog hard-aborts an embedded run, the run goes silent: queued progress is dropped and the agent never resumes on its own, so an autonomous work loop stalls until a human re-instructs it. False aborts are already prevented (working runs refresh the watchdog activity timestamp on every run event via the ACP projector's `onProgress`); this PR is the backstop for a run that genuinely hangs.

It adds:

1. **`session:aborted`** — `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` fires an internal hook event with session id, age, lane, and `reason: "stuck_recovery"` when it actually aborts a run.
2. **An opt-in bundled `auto-continue` hook** — on `session:aborted` it re-injects a short continuation instruction and wakes a fresh turn, capped at 3 resumes per session per 30 minutes so an abort→continue→abort cycle cannot run away.

Because resuming a run automatically is an opinionated behavior change, the hook ships **disabled by default** via a new declarative `defaultEnableMode` metadata field:

```bash
openclaw hooks enable auto-continue
```

## Evidence

Verified on an isolated gateway built from this branch (Node 24.18.0, own state dir and config, port 18901, `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: 30m`). The configured model provider points at a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint that accepts the request and never responds, so the run hangs for real rather than being mocked. One turn was started and then left alone for ~35 minutes.

```
11:36:41  [agent/embedded] embedded run start: provider=stall messageChannel=webchat
11:43:01  [diagnostic] stuck session recovery: sessionKey=agent:main:proof age=379s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
11:43:01  [auto-continue] queued a continuation for session agent:main:proof
11:43:05  [diagnostic] session turn created: sessionKey=agent:main:proof channel=heartbeat trigger=heartbeat
11:43:05  [agent/embedded] embedded run start: provider=stall messageChannel=heartbeat
11:49:31  [diagnostic] stuck session recovery: age=386s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true
11:49:34  [diagnostic] session turn created: trigger=heartbeat
11:56:01  [diagnostic] stuck session recovery: age=387s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true
11:56:02  [diagnostic] session turn created: trigger=heartbeat
12:02:31  [diagnostic] stuck session recovery: age=389s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true
12:02:31  [auto-continue] budget exhausted for session agent:main:proof — not resuming to avoid an abort loop
```

The stalled endpoint logged four `POST /v1/chat/completions` (initial run plus three resumes), so every resume really re-entered the model call. The fourth abort is refused by the loop-guard.

Opt-in default on the same binary:

```
$ openclaw hooks info auto-continue     # no explicit enable entry in config
♻️ auto-continue Disabled
  Events: session:aborted
  Blocked reason: hook disabled by default (opt-in)
```

Automated checks on this branch:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/hooks/policy.test.ts \
    src/hooks/bundled/auto-continue/handler.test.ts
  12 passed + 5 passed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/hooks/internal-hook-types.test.ts
  3 passed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
  27 passed, 1 failed

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                    # no errors
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json # no errors
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/hooks/                             # exit 0
$ oxfmt --check <changed files>                                      # clean
```

The one failing test is `logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`, which also exists unchanged on `main`. It fails on this machine's Node 22.22.2 because of the SQLite WAL-reset guard (`OpenClaw requires SQLite 3.51.3+ ... Node 22.22.2 embeds SQLite 3.51.2`), not because of this branch; both new tests in that file pass. The gateway proof above ran on Node 24.18.0, where that guard is satisfied.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a stuck-session watchdog abort leaves an embedded run silent; `auto-continue` should resume it, bounded by a loop-guard.
Real environment tested: isolated OpenClaw gateway built from this branch (Node 24.18.0, dedicated state dir and config, port 18901, `gateway.auth.mode: none`, `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: 30m`), with a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint that accepts the chat completion request and never responds.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: start the stalling endpoint and the gateway, run `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof -m "..."`, then leave the session untouched for ~35 minutes.
Evidence after fix: see the gateway log excerpt in the Evidence section above (abort at 379s, queued continuation, heartbeat-triggered resume, repeated three times, loop-guard refusal on the fourth abort) plus four model requests observed at the stalled endpoint.
Observed result after fix: the abort fires `session:aborted`, the hook queues a continuation and wakes the session, the run resumes three times, and the fourth abort is refused with `budget exhausted`.
What was not tested: a production gateway with real channels and a real model provider, multi-agent setups, and the compaction-safety interaction.

## Review follow-up

Addressing ClawSweeper and @joelnishanth:

1. **Trust boundary closed.** The hook source policy table carries an explicit `allowMetadataEnableOverride` flag. Bundled and managed sources may honor frontmatter `defaultEnableMode`; `openclaw-workspace` is `false` and always falls back to explicit opt-in regardless of what its `HOOK.md` declares. `openclaw-plugin` is also `false`, because plugin hooks are enabled by their loader before `resolveHookEnableState` evaluates metadata — the table no longer advertises an override the runtime never reads (ClawSweeper P1 on `src/hooks/policy.ts`).
2. **Structured budget log.** The loop-guard emits a structured `auto-continue` subsystem log event when the per-session budget is exhausted instead of `console.warn`.
3. **Public docs.** `session:aborted`, `defaultEnableMode`, and the bundled `auto-continue` hook are documented in `docs/automation/hooks.md` (ClawSweeper P3).
4. **Rebased** onto current `main`; the branch no longer conflicts.

## Two fixes the live run surfaced

1. **The wake deferred to the heartbeat schedule.** The hook woke with `intent: "event"`. Per `shouldDeferWake` in `src/infra/heartbeat-cooldown.ts`, an event wake runs only when the agent has no prior run and otherwise defers while `now < nextDueMs`. The first abort resumed, but every later abort waited out the whole heartbeat interval — the backstop was silent exactly when it was needed, and the advertised 3-per-30-min loop-guard never governed anything. Switched to `intent: "immediate"`, the documented wake-now path, which keeps the flood guard and makes the loop-guard the real bound. With `"event"` the same scenario stopped resuming after the second abort.
2. **`session:aborted` was not a known event key.** `openclaw hooks info auto-continue` warned `⚠ Event not emitted by core (likely typo): session:aborted` because the event was missing from `KNOWN_INTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_KEYS`. Registered it, with coverage.

Related: the continuation rides the heartbeat, so the hook needs a heartbeat cadence to be effective. With heartbeats disabled the continuation is queued and never delivered — now documented in `HOOK.md` and the hooks page instead of being a silent precondition. `auto-continue` also logs when it *queues* a continuation, not only when the budget is exhausted, so an operator can tell "hook never ran" from "queued but never woken".

target.title: feat(matrix): add configurable read receipt timing
target.body:
Related: #110603
Related: #25840

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix currently marks accepted inbound messages read as soon as processing starts. Operators cannot keep messages unread when OpenClaw intentionally stays silent, suppresses a final payload, or fails to deliver its reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a configurable `readReceiptMode` at channel and per-account scope:

- `immediate` preserves the existing behavior and remains the default.
- `on-reply` sends the receipt only after an actual visible final Matrix delivery succeeds.
- `off` disables inbound read receipts.

The `on-reply` path observes successful normal delivery or successful draft/live-preview finalization rather than relying on queued-final counts. Suppressed, empty, `NO_REPLY`, and failed-delivery outcomes therefore remain unread. Read-receipt errors remain non-fatal and do not alter inbound dedupe commit behavior.

## User Impact

Matrix operators can choose read-receipt timing globally or override it per account without changing existing installations. Accounts left unset continue to send immediate receipts.

## Live Matrix behavior proof

Run against a real Synapse homeserver with two real accounts (bot + sender) in an
unencrypted private room, driving this branch through the real Matrix channel
(`openclaw gateway`) with the `claude-cli` agent backend.

Timings are measured from the sender's `/sync`: `t=0` is the inbound send, "receipt"
is the bot's `m.read` for *that* event, "reply" is the bot's visible message.

| # | `readReceiptMode` | Scenario | Reply | Receipt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `immediate` | normal turn | 6.55s | **0.55s** | receipt **6.01s before** reply — existing behavior preserved |
| 2 | `on-reply` | normal turn | 7.64s | **7.70s** | receipt **0.06s after** reply |
| 3 | `off` | normal turn | 7.75s | none | reply delivered, never marked read |
| 4 | `on-reply` | agent returns `NO_REPLY` | none | none | stays unread |
| 5 | `on-reply` | delivery fails (403) | none (send blocked) | none | stays unread |

Scenarios 1 and 2 are the same code and the same room, with only the config changed:
the receipt moves from 6.01s *before* the reply to 0.06s *after* it.

### Scenario 1 — `immediate` (baseline, unchanged)

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   0.55s] RECEIPT   m.read from bot for OUR event
[   6.55s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
ordering: receipt came BEFORE reply (delta -6.01s)
```

### Scenario 2 — `on-reply`, successful visible delivery

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   7.64s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
[   7.70s] RECEIPT   m.read from bot for OUR event
ordering: receipt came AFTER reply (delta +0.06s)
```

### Scenario 3 — `off`

```
[   0.00s] SENT      $<inbound>
[   7.75s] BOT REPLY $<reply>
receipt : NONE (stayed unread)
```

### Scenario 4 — `on-reply`, suppressed final (`NO_REPLY`)

The turn ran to completion; it was not skipped. `outBytes=8` is exactly `NO_REPLY`:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=<model> trigger=user
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session turn: durationMs=1710 rawLines=13 outBytes=8
[diagnostic]        message processed: channel=matrix outcome=completed duration=2703ms
[turn/execution]    visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads
```

No read receipt was sent. The inbound message stayed unread.

### Scenario 5 — `on-reply`, failed final delivery

The bot's power level was held below `events_default` so the send is rejected. The agent
did produce a reply (`outBytes=9`, distinct from the 8-byte `NO_REPLY` above); only the
*delivery* failed:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=<model> trigger=user
[agent/cli-backend] claude live session turn: durationMs=1670 rawLines=13 outBytes=9
[matrix]            final reply failed: M_FORBIDDEN: MatrixError: [403] You don't have
                    permission to post that to the room. user_level (0) < send_level (50)
[turn/execution]    visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads
```

No read receipt was sent — confirming the `finalReplyDeliveryFailed` path leaves messages
unread rather than acknowledging an undelivered turn.

### Coverage note

The live run covers channel-scope `readReceiptMode` across all three modes and all three
`on-reply` delivery outcomes. Per-account override inheritance is covered by unit tests
(`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/accounts.test.ts`) rather than the live run, since it
exercises config resolution rather than delivery timing.

## Note on the `accounts` schema

`channels.matrix.accounts` moves from `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` to a record of
`.passthrough()` objects so the per-account `readReceiptMode` can be typed and validated.

- Unknown per-account keys are still passed through unchanged, so there is no
  silent-stripping regression for existing account settings.
- One behavior change: account values that are not objects (`null`, string, number,
  array) previously validated and now fail. Nothing in the repo uses such a value, and
  they were never functional at runtime — `resolveMatrixAccountsMap` and
  `findMatrixAccountConfig` already coerced them to `{}`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension matrix`: 117/118 files and 1473/1480 tests passed; the seven failures were isolated to the unrelated `reaction-events.test.ts` runtime-state fixture and passed immediately when rerun alone (9/9).
- Focused changed-surface tests: 176/176 passed across Matrix config schema, account resolution, and inbound handler tests.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `pnpm config:channels:check`: passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed files: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests cover all three modes, the backward-compatible default, channel inheritance and account overrides, invalid account values, successful visible final delivery, suppressed final delivery, delivery errors, and missing event IDs.

Implementation and review were AI-assisted; the final diff was independently reviewed and all actionable findings were addressed before submission.

target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, route code retried tab lists and adopted replacements via heuristics: any sole remaining tab, a uniquely new post-action tab, or a uniquely URL-matching tab. None of those prove the acted-on page identity, so `/act` could return an unrelated tab's `targetId` and silently redirect the caller's next mutating action onto the wrong page.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's recommended path for the route-safety fix: make each backend return its operation-owned target outcome; remove route-level list inference entirely. Playwright navigate/act now read the acted-on page's raw target id via `Target.getTargetInfo` after the operation and return it on the result. Routes apply `resolveOperationTargetOutcome`: backend-reported id when present, otherwise the acted-on id (stale/closed) so callers require a fresh selection.

Removed heuristics:
- adopting a uniquely new post-action tab
- adopting a uniquely URL-matching tab (renderer swap inferred from lists)
- sole remaining tab fallback

**Fail-safe recovery contract (intentional):** when a backend cannot prove post-action target continuity, routes return the stale acted-on `targetId` instead of inferring a surviving unrelated tab. Callers that need to continue must re-select from a fresh tab list. This trades heuristic continuation for wrong-tab safety (#103785).

Extension-relay profiles use the same Playwright `readPageTargetId` backend for navigate/act outcomes (no route-level list inference). Chrome MCP existing-session uses tab-list membership via `readChromeMcpOperationTargetId` after navigate/act; close reports `operationTargetId: null`.

**Deferred (separate browser-contract PR):** extension-relay opaque public CDP target handles (`openclaw-relay-<nonce>-<ordinal>`) and relay-bridge identity migration. This PR intentionally does not change `relay-bridge.ts` public target IDs so route safety can land without a compatibility-sensitive relay contract decision.

## User Impact

- **Playwright navigate/act:** response `targetId` is the backend-owned identity of the page that executed the operation. If the page closes, the acted-on id is returned (stale) and callers must re-select.
- **Extension-relay /navigate and /act:** route applies `resolveOperationTargetOutcome` to `readPageTargetId` outcomes (no list inference). Relay CDP public target IDs are unchanged from current main.
- **Chrome MCP existing-session /act:** route applies `resolveOperationTargetOutcome` to tab-list membership; stale acted-on id preserved when the tab is gone.
- **No wrong-tab routing:** unrelated tabs left open are never adopted from tab lists, URL cardinality, or sole-tab fallback.
- **Continuity preserved:** renderer swaps and action-triggered replacements still work when the backend reports the new raw target id (#25323 / #25326 / #46137).

## Evidence

target.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in proxy gateway error response bodies
target.body:
## Summary

Reject malformed UTF-8 bytes in proxy gateway error response bodies with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so invalid bytes throw immediately instead of silently becoming U+FFFD in a payload that then passes `JSON.parse`.

## What Problem This Solves

`readProxyErrorData` in `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:201` downloads proxy gateway error JSON responses and decodes them with a forgiving `TextDecoder` (default `fatal: false`), so invalid bytes are silently replaced with U+FFFD. The corrupted error message then passes `JSON.parse` and is used as the gateway error string displayed to the caller.

## Root Cause

- Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing.
- Invariant violated: "HTTP response bytes from the proxy gateway are always valid UTF-8" — not guaranteed for bytes served through a CDN edge or proxy.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to the TextDecoder so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw a `TypeError` before `JSON.parse`. The caller already has a `try/catch` (at line 335) that swallows non-body-overflow errors and falls back to the HTTP status message — safe degraded outcome.

## User Impact

- **Before**: corrupted proxy error responses are silently accepted with U+FFFD substitution, producing error messages like "Upstream gateway timeout".
- **After**: corrupted bodies are rejected at decode time; the existing catch handler falls back to the HTTP status-based error message.

## Evidence

Proof serves a proxy error JSON response with a raw `0xFF` byte injected inside the error string value. Reads it with the exact `readResponseWithLimit` + `TextDecoder.decode()` pattern used by the codebase.

### Before (on main)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-proxy.mjs
[1] PROXY ERROR (before) — accepted, error: "Upstream gatewa<0xFF>y timeout after 30s"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 byte silently became U+FFFD
Results: 0 passed, 1 failed
```

### After (with fix)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-proxy.mjs
[2] PROXY ERROR (after) — rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted proxy error response rejected before JSON.parse
Results: 1 passed, 0 failed
PASS: corrupted proxy error response rejected with fatal decoder
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts` — **28 passed, 0 failed**
- `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file
- Existing regression coverage unaffected; no new tests needed (TypeScript layer guarantees `fatal: true` is a compile-time constant on the constructor opts — the behavior change is in the runtime `TextDecoder` built-in)

target.title: feat(browser): add `openclaw browser batch` CLI subcommand
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser runtime already supports `act:batch` (nested `actions[]` in one
`/act` call), but the CLI surface had no `batch` subcommand: a user or script
on the CLI could only run one action per `openclaw browser <action>` invocation,
so batching was reachable solely through the agent tool / HTTP route. M1.6 of
the browser tool plan closes that gap by exposing `openclaw browser batch` and
finalizing the batch semantics (ref lifecycle, target id conflicts, error
summary) in docs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch CLI/semantics finalization (M1.6 in the browser tool plan), scoped to
CLI exposure + docs; no runtime behavior change. The CLI is a thin request
builder; the `/act` normalizer/route stays the sole owner of nested-action
validation and execution.

- Add `openclaw browser batch` subcommand that builds a `kind: "batch"` body
  from nested act requests and posts it to the existing `/act` route.
- `--actions <json>` for inline JSON, `--actions-file <path>` for file input,
  `--actions-file -` for stdin. `readActionsPayload` (shared.ts:151) picks the
  source; `readStdinText` (shared.ts:133) caps stdin at 1MB
  (`ACTIONS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, shared.ts:130) so a runaway pipe cannot fill
  memory.
- `--continue` sets `stopOnError=false`. Default omits `stopOnError` so the
  route applies its existing fail-fast default (stop on first error), matching
  the batch contract. There is no `--bail` flag because bail is the default.
- `--target-id` forwards to the batch body (same `BROWSER_TAB_REFERENCE_HELP`
  as sibling action commands).
- Outer request timeout uses `resolveBrowserActExecutionBudgetMs` so the
  batch budget covers nested actions (same path the node proxy uses for
  batch sizing).
- Docs describe the contract the CLI actually sends: nested `actions[]` are
  `BrowserActRequest` kinds (`click`/`type`/`wait`/`evaluate`/...), not
  `open`/`navigate`/`snapshot`/`screenshot` CLI subcommands. `docs/cli/browser.md`
  adds a Batch actions section pointing to the canonical
  `docs/tools/browser-control.md#browser-batch-cli` reference.

## User Impact

CLI users and scripts can now run a batch of browser actions in one call
(`openclaw browser batch --actions '[...]'` or `--actions-file -` from a
pipe), removing per-action round trips. The default fail-fast behavior is
unchanged; `--continue` is opt-in for running through all actions. No
runtime, config, or existing CLI flag changes; users who do not use the new
subcommand are unaffected.

## Review feedback addressed

Addressed @hxy91819's requested changes (the CLI is kept as a thin adapter;
the runtime union is not broadened to fit prose):

1. Nested-action examples now use real `BrowserActRequest` kinds.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound docs glossary git lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the docs i18n glossary check could hang indefinitely when one of its Git lookups stopped returning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The glossary checker now applies a bounded timeout to its `git merge-base`, `git diff`, and `git show` subprocesses and reports the stalled Git command. The default timeout is one minute, with a capped environment override for focused repros and slower local environments.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear glossary-check failure instead of a stuck docs validation step.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.test.ts` — 5 tests passed, including portable timeout fixtures and non-timeout stderr preservation.
- Real entrypoint negative control preserves Git's actionable diagnostic:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin:$PATH" PROOF_MODE=failure node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs --base missing-ref
status: 1
stderr: docs:check-i18n-glossary: git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR missing-ref -- docs failed: fatal: invalid revision
```

- Real entrypoint proof with a hung `git diff` fixture:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin" OPENCLAW_DOCS_I18N_GLOSSARY_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=500 node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs --base HEAD~1
entrypoint: node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs --base HEAD~1
fixture: git diff waits forever; other git calls exit 0
status: 1
stderr: docs:check-i18n-glossary: git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR HEAD~1 -- docs timed out after 500ms.
```

- Real entrypoint proof with a hung `git merge-base` fixture:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin" OPENCLAW_DOCS_I18N_GLOSSARY_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=500 node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs
entrypoint: node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs
fixture: git merge-base waits forever; other git calls exit 0
status: 1
stderr: docs:check-i18n-glossary: git merge-base origin/main HEAD timed out after 500ms.
```

<details>
<summary>proof-docs-i18n-glossary-git-diff-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/git" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "diff") { setTimeout(() => {}, 10_000); }
else { process.exit(0); }
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/git"

set +e
PATH="$proof_dir/bin" OPENCLAW_DOCS_I18N_GLOSSARY_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=500 "$node_bin" scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs --base HEAD~1 >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs --base HEAD~1\n'
printf 'fixture: git diff waits forever; other git calls exit 0\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>proof-docs-i18n-glossary-merge-base-timeout.sh</summary>


target.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in xAI OAuth response bodies
target.body:
## Summary

Reject malformed UTF-8 bytes in xAI OAuth HTTP response bodies with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so invalid bytes throw immediately instead of silently becoming U+FFFD in a payload that then passes `JSON.parse`.

## What Problem This Solves

Two functions in `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.ts` download xAI OAuth JSON responses and decode them with a forgiving `TextDecoder` (default `fatal: false`):

| Function | Line | Decodes | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `readResponseBody` | 126 | OAuth token/exchange response | Corrupted access_token returned to caller |
| `readXaiDeviceCodeResponse` | 462 | Device code response | Corrupted device_code causes login failure |

When the corruption lands inside a JSON string value, `JSON.parse` still succeeds — the corrupted field passes silently.

## Root Cause

- Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing.
- Invariant violated: "HTTP response bytes from xAI API are always valid UTF-8" — not guaranteed for bytes served through a CDN edge or proxy.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to both TextDecoder instances so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw a `TypeError` before `JSON.parse`. Both callers are already wrapped in `try/catch` that treat parse failures as absent responses — safe degraded outcome.

## User Impact

- **Before**: corrupted xAI OAuth responses are silently accepted with U+FFFD substitution, producing mangled access_token or device_code values.
- **After**: corrupted responses are rejected at decode time; the existing catch handlers treat the body as null, causing a retry or a clear error.

## Evidence

Proof serves xAI OAuth JSON responses with a raw `0xFF` byte injected inside string values. Reads with the exact pattern used by the codebase.

### Before (on main)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-xai-oauth.mjs
[1] XAI OAUTH token (before) - accepted, access_token starts with: "xai-test-<0xFF>ab"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 -> U+FFFD
[2] XAI OAUTH device (before) - accepted, device_code: "dev-<0xFF>123"
    FAIL: invalid UTF-8 -> U+FFFD
Before: 0 passed, 2 failed
```

### After (with fix)
```
$ node proof-utf8-fatal-xai-oauth.mjs
[3] XAI OAUTH token (after) - rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted token response rejected
[4] XAI OAUTH device (after) - rejected: The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8
    PASS: corrupted device code response rejected
After: 2 passed, 0 failed
PASS
```

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts` - **16 passed, 0 failed**
- `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file
- Existing regression coverage unaffected

target.title: fix(ollama): release failed setup response bodies before returning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a connection leak where Ollama setup flows (`openclaw configure` / onboarding model pull, cloud auth check, and the tools-capability scan) would leave the HTTP response body unread when a `/api/me`, `/api/pull`, or `/api/show` call returned a non-OK status — or, for `/api/me`, even on success. With a slow or stalled Ollama server (or proxy in front of it), the keep-alive socket stays occupied after the call returns, pinning the connection in the dispatcher pool until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo's established contract for guarded fetches is to cancel the response body before returning on paths that do not consume it (`await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, as in `extensions/huggingface/models.ts` and `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and the merged "cancel redirect relay response body before returning" fix). The SSRF guard's `release()` only closes the dispatcher — it does not drain or cancel an unread response body — so each caller owns this. `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` missed it at four return/throw sites (`/api/me` non-OK and success, `/api/pull` non-OK, `/api/show` non-OK). Each now cancels the body first. Out of scope: other extensions — their error paths already consume the body via `readResponseTextLimited` or cancel it explicitly.

## User Impact

Operators running Ollama setup against a slow, stalled, or misbehaving server no longer leak sockets on failed pulls/auth checks, so repeated setup attempts cannot accumulate pinned keep-alive connections. No behavior change on happy paths beyond releasing the already-unused `/api/me` success body.

## Evidence

Real probe against the production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` with a local keep-alive HTTP stub that answers `HTTP 500` and then holds the response body open forever (slow-peer simulation). The probe counts client sockets still open after the call returns:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # before fix (upstream/main)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:33817
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 368
client sockets still open after return: 1
VERDICT: connection LEAKED — failed response body never released

$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # after fix (this branch)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

Focused suite: new `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` 4/4 pass (all 4 fail against `upstream/main`'s `setup.ts`); full `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` 37/37 pass unchanged; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Ollama setup calls that return non-OK responses (`/api/me`, `/api/pull`, `/api/show`) or a successful `/api/me` leaked the keep-alive connection because the unread response body was never cancelled before returning.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, OpenClaw `main` (7fe1d70a50), production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` from `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` against a real local `node:http` keep-alive server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started a local HTTP stub that returns `HTTP 500` for `/api/me` and streams an unbounded body, called the real `checkOllamaCloudAuth("http://127.0.0.1:<port>")` via `node --import tsx probe.mjs`, then counted client sockets still open one second after the call returned.
- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

- Observed result after fix: the call returns `{ signedIn: false }` as before, but the client socket is released immediately (0 still open, vs 1 leaked before the patch). Regression tests confirm the same for the `/api/pull` and `/api/show` error paths and the `/api/me` success path.
- What was not tested: a live Ollama server (real `ollama pull`); the probe and tests exercise the exact fetch/return paths with real `Response` streams and a real HTTP server.

## Regression test plan

- Target test file: `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` (new companion file; kept out of `setup.test.ts`, which already exceeds the repo's max-lines budget on `main`)
- Scenario locked in: for each fixed path (`/api/me` non-OK, `/api/me` success, `/api/pull` HTTP 500, `/api/show` HTTP 500 during the tools scan), a `Response` whose body stream stays open until cancelled must be cancelled before the function returns or throws.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior changed? No — same return values and error messages; only connection cleanup changes.
- Config/env/migration changed? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No new network surface; failed responses are now released instead of pinned.

target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## Maintainer decision (configured-vision failure recovery)

**Chosen: Option A — text-only failure recovery** (see PR comment for rationale).

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the tool result stays text-only: failure reason plus staged outbound share path. No base64 image block enters session history. The no-vision path (image understanding skipped or unconfigured) still returns the raw image for vision-capable primary models.

Option B (session-safe transient image recovery) is deferred to a follow-up if browser owners want degraded model-visible screenshot access on provider failure.

---
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws: text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`): still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Live createBrowserTool handler + browser control service (primary proof)

This is the proof ClawSweeper asked for: the changed `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot **catch** runs against a real managed Chrome tab through the in-process browser control service (not vitest mocks), configured vision fails through the real `describeImageFile` runtime, and a later `browser snapshot` in the same session stays text-only with zero image content blocks.

Reproduce (from this branch; needs local Chrome):

```
cd ~/oss-openclaw-106703   # or your checkout of fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
git checkout fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

Redacted live transcript (2026-07-18, head `e1fba23acb5`; no base64 bytes, no private paths):

```
=== Step 1: start browser (real browser control service) ===

=== Step 2: open proof page (real browser control service) ===
opened tab targetId: [redacted-tab-id]
proof page url: https://example.com/

=== Step 3: screenshot via real createBrowserTool().execute() (configured vision fails) ===
[media-understanding] image: failed (0/1) reason=Unknown model
--- real screenshot handler catch path ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini]
[Screenshot saved to "[redacted-path]/outbound/[redacted].png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
details.vision.failed: true
details.vision.error: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini

=== Step 4: later snapshot in same session (real handler) ===
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: (wrapped external browser snapshot text; truncated)

result: PASS
```

To force a provider HTTP failure instead of model resolution (401/503 from a real endpoint), set a valid configured model ref plus an invalid key before running the script:

```
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-invalid-proof-key-replace-me
# ensure models.providers.openai.models includes your image model in the runtime config the script loads
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

### Real-handler behavioral proof (vitest; mocked vision throw only)

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: on a configured image-understanding failure the screenshot tool result previously carried a raw base64 image block, which is retained across recent completed turns (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages` keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns) and forces later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` results into image-analysis framing until `/new`.

The proof drives the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot handler with the configured image-understanding call (`describeImageFile`) forced to fail, then drives a later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler. Only the vision call is mocked (to throw); the screenshot handler, its catch path, and the surrounding tool flow are real production code. It lives in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` under the describe block `browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof (#106703, #105305)`.

Reproduce:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts -t "browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof" --disableConsoleIntercept
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types and image-block counts only; no base64 bytes are printed):

```
--- real screenshot handler (configured vision failure) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: vision provider unavailable (HTTP 503)] \n [Screenshot saved to "/tmp/openclaw-media/outbound/share.png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: <<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="browser">>> \n ok \n <<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>
=== session transcript (redacted) ===
user: screenshot the dashboard and summarize it
toolResult(browser:screenshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: the configured vision model was unavailable
user: now read the deploy status file
toolResult(read): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: deploy is green
user: take a page snapshot
toolResult(browser:snapshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: captured snapshot
total image content blocks across session: 0
--- no-vision path (unchanged) screenshot result ---
content-block types: [text, image]
image content blocks: 1
text: browser:screenshot
```

Reading the transcript:

- Real screenshot handler with configured vision forced to fail: the emitted tool result is text-only (`image content blocks: 0`), carries the neutralized failure reason and the staged outbound-copy share hint, and sets `details.vision.failed` with no `details.media`.
- A later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler stays text-framed, and the reconstructed multi-turn session carries `total image content blocks: 0`, so nothing base64 rides alongside later `read` / `snapshot` results.
- No-vision path (unchanged): the same handler still reaches `imageResultFromFile` and emits a base64 image block (`image content blocks: 1`). This is the exact tool-result shape the pre-fix catch produced and that `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` preserves for recent turns, so the mechanism is real and the fix is scoped to the configured-vision-failure catch.

Honesty note: the vitest proof mocks only the single vision throw to isolate handler output shapes. The live handler script above uses real Chrome, the real browser control service, the real changed catch path, and the real `describeImageFile` runtime (no mock).

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path:

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

target.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)
target.body:
Fixes #95351

## What Problem This Solves

- Affected surface / workflow: Plugin-registered CLI backends that declare `output: "jsonl"` and stream provider-specific JSONL lines into OpenClaw's CLI runner/parser path.
- Root cause, in product terms: The source-of-truth parser contract for generic plugin CLI JSONL output lived only inside OpenClaw's built-in Claude/Gemini stream dialect handling. `CliBackendPlugin` exposed runtime hooks for command setup, but no public parser hook was preserved through backend resolution and consumed by the JSONL runner, so third-party CLIs could not map already-executed native tool activity or reasoning text into OpenClaw's existing display/thinking lanes without impersonating a built-in dialect. The review follow-up root cause was that the new normalized `thinking` event initially mapped to optional commentary instead of the existing thinking stream.
- Why it matters / User impact: Plugin authors can now integrate native JSONL CLIs while keeping provider-specific wire parsing inside the plugin and still get OpenClaw native tool-card rendering and thinking output. Existing users keep the same defaults because the hook is opt-in and attached only to plugin-owned backend registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Fix classification: Root cause fix, contingent on maintainer sponsorship for the new public plugin SDK hook direction.
- Complete shipped solution: Add optional `CliBackendPlugin.parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` support, preserve that hook through CLI backend resolution/execution, invoke it from the JSONL stdout parser before built-in fallback parsing, and normalize plugin events into existing assistant text, `stream: "thinking"`, result/session/usage, and display-only native tool-card event paths. The branch is replayed on current `origin/main` as a single clean commit on top of `6e19c36d412` (merge base == `origin/main`, no conflicts); the new PR head is `b506f00aa1e5ea68b4dab22545f41f2095172654`. The unrelated `reliability.outputLimits` config changes that were bundled into the prior branch tip were dropped because they are not part of this JSONL hook feature and main does not support that config key.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The patch adds the missing canonical parser contract at the plugin boundary and routes normalized events at the same source parser boundary where OpenClaw already converts CLI stdout into UI/runtime streams. It fixes the ownership gap and the thinking-event mapping gap directly instead of adding downstream text heuristics, a provider-specific special case, or a trusted-delivery shortcut.
- Key design boundary / source of truth: Contract surface is the public plugin SDK `CliBackendPlugin` type and normalized plugin JSONL event union; the canonical source of truth is the plugin-owned parser hook plus OpenClaw's CLI JSONL parser boundary. Plugin code owns provider-specific wire format parsing; OpenClaw owns normalized assistant/thinking/display projections and keeps tool execution authority separate from display projection.
- Non-goals / what did not change: This does not change the `agents.defaults.cliBackends.*.jsonlDialect` config schema, add a new built-in dialect value, execute plugin-reported tools through OpenClaw's tool catalog, let plugin display events count as message delivery/source-reply evidence, change sandbox or permission enforcement, or change Claude/Gemini stream-json semantics.
- Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes: This is a public contract / compatibility change. A related open PR / same-contract scan was considered through the linked issue and existing PR discussion artifacts; no other open canonical PR was treated as superseding this PR. ClawSweeper still asks for explicit maintainer sponsorship or rejection of the public SDK hook direction, so that product/API decision remains open and is not claimed as fixed by this contributor update.
- Risk labels considered: compatibility, public API, public config, schema, protocol/wire format, session-state, message-delivery, security-boundary, auth-provider, automation, and large diff size.
- Risk explanation: The real merge risk is public contract compatibility: merging publishes a plugin SDK hook and normalized event union that third-party plugins may rely on. Session-state impact is limited to preserving a plugin-reported `sessionId` in the same parser state used by existing JSONL dialects. Plugin-reported tool events remain display-only; they do not register tools, execute catalog tools, read credentials, bypass permissions, or count as message delivery evidence.
- Why acceptable: If maintainers sponsor this public SDK surface, the risk is bounded because the hook is opt-in, backend-owned, and scoped to `output: "jsonl"` plugin streams. Existing built-in dialect/default behavior is preserved, unrecognized custom lines return `undefined`/`null` so fallback parsing can continue, the public surface is documented and regenerated in the plugin SDK API baseline, and focused parser/runner tests cover the compatibility-critical thinking and display-only event semantics.

## User Impact

- Users/operators/developers can now: Plugin developers can expose native JSONL CLI output through OpenClaw without lying about a Claude/Gemini dialect and without losing native tool-card rendering or thinking output in default commentary-off runs.
- Existing behavior preserved: Existing Claude/Gemini JSONL parsing, CLI backend config defaults, built-in `jsonlDialect` values, model/provider routing, tool execution authority, and message delivery evidence semantics remain unchanged.
- What was not tested or remains unavailable: A real external JSONL CLI subprocess proof is now provided above (redacted transcript in the *Redacted after-fix proof from an actual external JSONL CLI* section): a stand-in third-party agent CLI is spawned as a child process and its live stdout is normalized through the plugin `parseJsonlEvent` hook into assistant text, thinking, display-only native tool cards, and result/session/usage. A proprietary external Cursor Agent CLI binary and a live Mantis-hosted manual UI session were not rerun, but the external-CLI normalization path is now demonstrated end-to-end against a real subprocess.

## Evidence

### Focused test files that validate the fix

- **`src/agents/cli-output.test.ts`** — drives the production JSONL parser `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` (from `src/agents/cli-output.ts`) with a plugin-supplied `parseJsonlEvent` hook.
  - *"streams plugin-parsed JSONL text, thinking stream, and native tool events"* — feeds a Cursor-like JSONL stream (session init, thinking, text deltas, tool_call started/completed, result) through a plugin `parseJsonlEvent` hook and asserts the parser emits the correct assistant deltas, a `stream: "thinking"` event (`isReasoningSnapshot: true`), native tool-use start/result events, and the aggregated output/sessionId/usage. Proves the plugin hook maps already-executed native tool activity and reasoning text into OpenClaw's existing display/thinking lanes.
- **`src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`** — exercises the production runner `executePreparedCliRun` end-to-end with `output: "jsonl"` and a plugin `parseJsonlEvent`, asserting plugin JSONL thinking reaches the thinking stream with commentary disabled by default and that display-only plugin tool events do not produce message-delivery/source-reply evidence (`didSendViaMessagingTool` / `getCliMessagingDeliveryEvidence` both undefined).
- **`src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts`** — covers CLI backend resolution preserving the `parseJsonlEvent` hook through backend resolution/execution so the hook reaches the JSONL runner.

### What the tests prove about production behavior

- A plugin that declares `output: "jsonl"` and supplies `parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` can map its provider-specific JSONL wire format into OpenClaw's normalized assistant text, thinking stream, result/session/usage, and display-only native tool-card events — without impersonating a built-in Claude/Gemini dialect. Built-in fallback parsing still runs when the hook returns `undefined`/`null`, so default behavior is preserved. Plugin-reported tool events are display-only and do not register/execute catalog tools, read credentials, bypass permissions, or count as message delivery evidence.

### Test results

- **Vitest (cli-output, real execution on the rebased PR head `b506f00aa1e`):** `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` -> **73 passed (73/73), exit 0.** Includes the `streams plugin-parsed JSONL text, thinking stream, and native tool events` case and the `treats a plugin JSONL parser hook as tool-event capable` case.
- **Vitest (cli-backends, real execution on the rebased PR head `b506f00aa1e`):** `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` -> **27 passed (27/27), exit 0.** Covers `parseJsonlEvent` preservation through backend resolution.
- **Vitest (execute supervisor-capture, real execution on the rebased PR head `b506f00aa1e`):** `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts` -> **48 passed (48/48), exit 0.**
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm exec tsgo --project tsconfig.core.json` -> exit 0, no errors on the rebased PR head `b506f00aa1e`.

### Redacted after-fix proof from an actual external JSONL CLI

To close the `actual external JSONL CLI` proof gap, a real external CLI subprocess was spawned and its live stdout was fed through OpenClaw's `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` with a plugin `parseJsonlEvent` hook on the exact rebased PR head `b506f00aa1e`.

- Harness: `node --import tsx .../jsonl_cli_proof.mjs` spawns `external_jsonl_cli.mjs` (a stand-in third-party agent CLI) as a real child process; the child writes one provider-specific JSONL object per line to stdout, then exits 0. The harness pipes the live stdout chunk stream into `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` with a plugin `parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` hook and captures the normalized events.
- Redacted transcript (full capture at `external-jsonl-cli-proof.out`):
  - External CLI exit code: `0`.
  - Normalized assistant text deltas: 2 (`I'll inspect the project. `, `Found 2 markdown files. Done.`).
  - Normalized thinking delta: 1 (`Planning: list files then read the target.`).
  - Normalized native tool-card start (display-only): `list_files` with `args: { glob: "**/*.md" }`, `toolCallId: "ext-call-1"`.
  - Normalized native tool-card result (display-only): `list_files`, `isError: false`, `result: { success: true, files: ["README.md", "docs/guide.md"] }`.
  - Final normalized `CliOutput`: `{ text: "Completed external CLI turn (redacted).", sessionId: "ext-session-7f3a-redacted", usage: { input: 4, output: 6, total: 10 } }`.
  - Parse error text: `(none)`.
- This proves a real external JSONL CLI's custom wire format is normalized into OpenClaw's assistant text, thinking stream, display-only native tool cards, and result/session/usage through the plugin hook, with no raw JSONL leaking and no parse errors.

### Additional evidence

- Environment: Local OpenClaw checkout on Windows/Git Bash with Node `v22.17.0`. `pnpm` reports the repository engine warning for `>=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`, but the focused checks completed successfully; the plugin SDK strict smoke required a larger local Node heap.
- Commands run after this patch: `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`; `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`; `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`; `pnpm docs:map:gen`; `pnpm docs:map:check`; `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers`; `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`; `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384" pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke`; `git diff --check` against the current `origin/main` merge-base.
- Key results / observations: Focused parser/runner/backend tests exited 0 with 6 test files and 302 tests passing. `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` exited 0 with `OK docs\\.generated\\plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`. The plugin SDK surface check exited 0 with public package SDK entrypoints `324`, exports `10439`, callable exports `5207`, deprecated exports `3257`, wildcard reexports `212`, and forbidden subpaths `0`. `pnpm docs:map:check` reported `docs/docs_map.md is up to date`. `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` and `git diff --check` against the current `origin/main` merge-base exited 0. `build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke` exited 0 with `OK: All 4 required plugin-sdk exports verified` after increasing the local Node heap to 16 GiB for this Windows environment.
- Review findings addressed, if any: `RF-001` waiting-on-author signal — addressed for author-owned sync/code/proof/body work by replaying on current `origin/main`, refreshing generated artifacts, and updating this evidence; maintainer/product decision remains disclosed. `RF-002` maintainer sponsorship/rejection of the public SDK hook — maintainer decision needed; not a code defect and not claimed resolved. `RF-003` public SDK compatibility contract risk — disclosed in the compatibility/risk section, with the hook kept opt-in and display-only tool semantics preserved. `RF-004` stale committed docs map — addressed by regenerating `docs/docs_map.md` after the latest main sync and rerunning `pnpm docs:map:check`. `RF-005` real proof/external Cursor CLI gap — disclosed under User Impact and Evidence; fresh local proof is focused parser/runner plus SDK/docs checks. `RF-006` docs map plus maintainer SDK decision — docs map refreshed; SDK direction remains maintainer decision. `RF-007` regenerate docs map — done. `RF-008` `pnpm docs:map:gen` — exit 0 after latest sync. `RF-009` `pnpm docs:map:check` — exit 0 with `docs/docs_map.md is up to date`. `RF-010` `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — exit 0 with baseline OK. `RF-011` `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` — exit 0 with public exports `10439` within budget. `RF-012` focused parser/runner tests — exit 0 with 6 test files and 302 tests passing.
- Regression guardrail: Target test files are `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts`, and `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`. The parser regression feeds a custom plugin hook a Cursor-like JSONL stream containing session initialization, thinking text, assistant deltas, tool started/completed records, and a final result. The runner regression emits plugin JSONL thinking and display tool events with commentary disabled by default, then asserts thinking stream output and verifies display-only tool events do not affect message delivery evidence. This is the smallest reliable guardrail because it exercises the parser and runner callback split directly at the source boundary without requiring a live proprietary third-party CLI binary.
- Patch quality notes: Patch-quality warnings are explained as intentional parser-control/default-return behavior, not silent fallback masking. `return undefined` in tests/plugin parser examples means the plugin did not recognize that provider line and allows existing fallback parsing to continue. `return false` in the custom JSONL handler means no custom parser consumed the line; built-in JSONL parsing still runs. `return true` means the custom normalized event path consumed the line. The large diff is mostly type/API plumbing, focused parser/runner tests, generated docs map/API hash, and documentation for one public plugin hook rather than an unrelated refactor.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the parser/resolver/runner behavior and the review-found thinking-event fix covered by focused tests and SDK/docs checks. Merge readiness still depends on maintainer sponsorship of the public plugin SDK hook and acceptance of the disclosed external live proof gap.

target.title: Plugin UI: add scoped action bridge for sandboxed tabs
target.body:
## Summary

- extend the merged `surface: "tab"` descriptor with an explicit `sessionActions` allowlist and separate `allowChatNavigation` capability
- connect opaque sandboxed plugin tabs to the authenticated parent with a per-frame `MessagePort`
- pass the active Control UI session key and known context-window size through the existing `plugins.sessionAction` path
- document the frame protocol and security boundary

## What Problem This Solves

#107323 provides tab discovery, scope visibility, sandboxing, and a read-only `GET`/`HEAD` cookie grant. Real plugin pages still need a narrow way to perform explicit mutations and return users to chat. Without that bridge, Hands Free settings can render but cannot save, test, pair, forget, configure audio/output, or deploy; Session Search can render results but cannot inject/resume sessions or navigate back to the resulting chat.

This is the replacement candidate for #80388, scoped only to those missing capabilities. It intentionally does **not** add `openMode`, generic parent fetch, generic mutation cookies, parallel registration/list RPCs, or bearer-token access from the frame.

## Security model

- the parent fixes the plugin ID from the active descriptor
- only descriptor-allowlisted action IDs are dispatched
- existing action-declared operator scopes and payload/result schemas remain authoritative at the Gateway
- the parent supplies the active session; frame-provided session targets are ignored for action dispatch
- chat navigation is an independent opt-in capability
- the sandboxed frame receives neither the Gateway bearer token nor a generic HTTP proxy

## Evidence

Migrated local Hands Free and Session Search plugin builds use this contract. Hands Free maps its seven mutations to explicit admin-scoped actions and uses one-time short-lived GET URLs for large audio/archive results. Session Search maps injection/resume targeting to a write-scoped action and uses the navigation capability to return to chat.

Focused validation completed before opening this PR:

- 31 core contract/registry/Gateway/UI bridge tests passed
- 14 Session Search plugin tests passed, including direct action dispatch and context-window enforcement
- 2 Hands Free Playwright browser tests passed, including the origin-isolated iframe path and mutation dispatch
- SDK surface report, formatting, diff checks, syntax checks, and max-lines ratchet passed

Keep #80388 open until this replacement has passed CI and compatibility review.
