target.title: fix(qqbot): settle RESUME watermark after handler completes without removing ingress lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #109996

Replaces #109997 — this branch applies the same SeqWatermark fix while preserving the QQ Bot ingress lifecycle end to end.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where queued or in-flight QQ Bot gateway messages are lost when the WebSocket reconnects or restarts. On current main, the RESUME `seq` is set to the latest received frame sequence number immediately upon receipt. If a message has been received but its handler has not yet completed (queued behind other messages, waiting for admission, or mid-processing), a reconnect or restart replays from that seq — **skipping the in-flight message permanently**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix introduces a `SeqWatermark` that delays the settlement of a message frame's sequence number until the queued message handler completes. The watermark exposes two cursors:

- `latest()` — the highest received frame seq, for heartbeat reporting (so the server doesn't think the client is behind)
- `value()` — the resumable seq (highest settled seq, or just below the oldest unsettled message)

**Critical**: this branch preserves the QQ Bot ingress lifecycle intact (unlike #109997, which removed `createQQBotIngressMonitor` / `QQBotIngressLifecycle` / `turnAdoptionLifecycle`). `gatewaySeq` tracking uses a FIFO `pendingTurnSeqs` queue — turn-event seqs are registered in frame order (via `handleSocketMessage`) and settled in the same order (ingress processes sequentially, queue drains FIFO). No lifecycle removal.

Changes:
- New `SeqWatermark` class with `register`/`settle`/`observe`/`latest`/`value` (+tests)
- `onMessageSettled` callback on the message queue — called in `processOne` `finally` block when any handler completes or fails
- `settleMessage` dequeues from `pendingTurnSeqs` so merged group turns settle every source seq
- Heartbeats report `seqWatermark.latest()` (receive cursor) instead of `lastSeq` (watermark)
- RESUME and persistence use `seqWatermark.value()` (settled cursor)

## User Impact

QQ Bot operators no longer lose messages on reconnect or restart. Messages received by the gateway but still in-flight (queued, waiting for admission, or mid-processing) are replayed after reconnection instead of silently dropped.

## Evidence

### SeqWatermark unit tests (8 tests)

New `seq-watermark.test.ts` covers: empty/seed, immediate observe, unsettled hold, out-of-order settling, latest vs value, reset.

### Gateway integration tests

All existing `gateway-connection.test.ts` (10 tests) and `message-queue.test.ts` (8 tests) continue to pass. The ingress lifecycle code was not modified — `dispatchIngressMessage`, `createQQBotIngressMonitor`, `shutdown`, and `handleSocketMessage` all retain their existing behavior.

### Key design: FIFO pendingTurnSeqs queue

Turn-event seqs are registered in `handleSocketMessage` (frame order) and dequeued in `settleMessage` (handler completion order). This works because the ingress and queue both process sequentially — the registration order matches the settlement order. No cross-message state is shared beyond the watermark itself.

### Compared with the rejected PR #109997

| Aspect | #109997 (rejected) | This PR |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| Ingress lifecycle | Removed entirely | Preserved intact |
| `dispatchIngressMessage` | Deleted | Unchanged |
| Seq tracking | `gatewaySeq` on message | FIFO `pendingTurnSeqs` in GatewayConnection |
| Shutdown/recovery | Replaced | Preserved |
| Test coverage | 27 new tests (340 lines changed) | 8 new SeqWatermark tests; all existing tests pass |

### Sibling-surface audit

- Only QQ Bot gateway module affected (`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/`)
- `message-queue.ts`: added `onMessageSettled` optional callback — called in `finally`, no behavioral change for callers who don't pass it
- No other channel plugins or gateway modules reference seq tracking or the QQ Bot ingress lifecycle

### Format

`pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passes on all four changed files.

target.title: fix(agents): allow configless gateway rebind to activate standalone owner
target.body:
Fixes #111520

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operator admins on a configless gateway (no explicit model in `openclaw.json`, model resolved from a provider env key like `OPENAI_API_KEY`) are permanently stuck on the Control UI Model Setup page. Clicking "Test & use" fails with:

```
Connection failed: prepared model runtime owner was not committed after replacement
```

Because activation never commits, `openclaw.setup.detect` keeps returning `setupComplete: false`, so every admin device is bounced to `/settings/model-setup?firstRun=1` from the default chat landing. On a multi-user trusted-proxy gateway this locks all admins out of the chat UI.

The only workaround is host-side CLI (`openclaw models set openai/gpt-5.6-sol` + gateway restart), which regular Control UI users cannot perform.

## Why This Change Was Made

`acquirePreparedModelRuntimeLease` unconditionally calls `rebindInputToCommittedConfiguredOwner` when the gateway lifecycle is active and the requesting path has `provenance: "run"`. On a configless gateway, no `provenance: "configured"` owner exists, so rebind throws `PreparedModelRuntimeOwnerNotPublishedError` with no fallback.

The sibling path `loadPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshot` already handles this by catching the same error and falling through to `activateStandalonePreparedModelRuntime`. This change adds a parallel guard in `acquirePreparedModelRuntimeLease`: catch the error, verify the requesting runtime has no matching configured owner (to preserve the error for stale-owner refresh), then let the raw input proceed to standalone lease publication.

The fallback predicate was refined from "any configured owner exists in the process" to "a configured owner matches this runtime's identity/directory", so a mixed gateway (one configured agent + one configless runtime) no longer incorrectly blocks the configless runtime.

## User Impact

Operator admins on configless gateways can now complete Model Setup "Test & use" directly through the Control UI without host-side CLI intervention. The setup flow detects the provider-derived model, live-tests it, persists the config, and marks setup complete — all from the browser.

## Evidence

### Before fix

Gateway with empty `openclaw.json`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` set via env. Model Setup "Test & use" → error:

```
Connection failed: prepared model runtime owner was not committed after replacement for /home/openclaw/.openclaw/agents/main/agent
```

`setup.detect` continues reporting `setupComplete: false`, redirect loop persists.

### After fix — real gateway proof

Started a clean-state gateway with no `openclaw.json` and a fake `OPENAI_API_KEY`:

```bash
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof-111841 \
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proof-fake-key-111841 \
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18790 --auth token --token proof-token-111841 --allow-unconfigured
```

Gateway resolved the default model from the env key and became ready:

```
[gateway] agent model: openai/gpt-5.6-sol (thinking=medium, fast=off)
[gateway] ready
```

`openclaw.setup.detect` found the OpenAI API-key candidate:

```bash
node openclaw.mjs gateway call --url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 --token proof-token-111841 --json \
  openclaw.setup.detect --params '{}'
```

```json
{
  "candidates": [
    { "kind": "openai-api-key", "modelRef": "openai/gpt-5.6", "credentials": true }
  ],
  "setupComplete": false
}
```

`openclaw.setup.activate` (Model Setup "Test & use") proceeded past prepared-runtime activation and reached the provider call instead of failing with the lifecycle error:

```bash
node openclaw.mjs gateway call --url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 --token proof-token-111841 --json --timeout 60000 \
  openclaw.setup.activate --params '{"kind":"openai-api-key"}'
```

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "status": "auth",
  "error": "403 Country, region, or territory not supported"
}
```

The request did **not** fail with `prepared model runtime owner was not committed after replacement`; it failed only at the provider auth step, which is expected with a fake/redacted key and confirms the configless runtime activated successfully.

### Unit tests

```
✓ src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.test.ts — 26 passed
✓ src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.lifecycle.test.ts — 40 passed (66 total)
```

Includes a new regression test: a configless runtime activates standalone while another agent is configured.

target.title: feat(openrouter): forward OpenClaw session id as session_id
target.body:
Optionally forward a stable, OpenRouter-scoped session identifier to OpenRouter as the chat-completion session_id body field. OpenRouter uses it as a sticky routing key (better prompt-cache hits) and for observability. Opt-in per the OpenRouter plugin config (forwardSessionId), off by default; the forwarded value is a SHA-256 hash derived from the active OpenClaw session id (not the raw internal identifier), fits well within OpenRouter's 256-char cap, and never overrides a caller-set value. **Update:** Following ClawSweeper's review, this now forwards an opaque derived identifier instead of the raw OpenClaw session id, per its P1 recommendation ("Derive an OpenRouter-scoped value before merge"). See the "Updated proof" note in the Real behavior proof section below. ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? * OpenRouter accepts a `session_id` to route requests to the same upstream provider, which maximizes prompt-cache hits and improves observability[cite: 1]. * OpenClaw already generates a stable per-session ID, but it was not being forwarded to OpenRouter[cite: 1]. Why does this matter now? * Forwarding the session ID allows OpenRouter to keep a multi-turn OpenClaw session on one upstream provider[cite: 1]. * This improves cache economics and traceability for users[cite: 1]. What is the intended outcome? * Optionally forward a stable, OpenRouter-scoped identifier derived from the active OpenClaw session ID to OpenRouter as the `session_id` request-body field on chat-completion calls[cite: 1]. * This feature is opt-in, configured per model provider (OpenRouter) via the OpenRouter plugin config, and is off by default[cite: 1]. * The derived value is a fixed 64-character SHA-256 hex digest, well under OpenRouter's 256-character limit[cite: 1]. * If a caller-set value already exists, it is never overridden[cite: 1]. What is intentionally out of scope? * Image, music, video, media-understanding, or speech OpenRouter providers (this is for chat/text inference only)[cite: 1]. * Generic provider session forwarding (this is an OpenRouter-specific field)[cite: 1]. * Changing core SDK context types or the shared transport turn-state hook[cite: 1]. * Sending the `x-session-id` header (the body field is sufficient and takes precedence)[cite: 1]. What does success look like? * When enabled, the `session_id` is injected into the OpenRouter chat-completion body[cite: 1]. * When disabled, there is no change to existing behavior (byte-identical payloads)[cite: 1]. What should reviewers focus on? * The implementation in `extensions/openrouter/stream.ts`, specifically the payload-patch wrapper[cite: 1]. * The addition of the boolean flag in the OpenRouter plugin's `configSchema` (`extensions/openrouter/openclaw.plugin.json`)[cite: 1]. * The edge case handling (flag off, caller-set value, over-long ID)[cite: 1].
Summary guidance This PR description is the contributor's durable explanation of the change. Write it for human maintainers first; ClawSweeper and Barnacle use the same text to understand intent, proof, risk, and current review state. Describe the intent and outcome in 2-5 bullets. Avoid restating the diff; reviewers and bots can read the changed files. If this PR fixes a plugin beta-release blocker, title it `fix(): beta blocker - ` and link the matching `Beta blocker: - ` issue labeled `beta-blocker`. Contributors cannot label PRs, so the title is the PR-side signal for maintainers and automation.
## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes # Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? Related # Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?
Linked context guidance Link the issue, PR, discussion, maintainer request, or owner request that explains why this PR should exist. Maintainer context helps reviewers and automation distinguish intended work from drive-by churn.
## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Forwarding OpenClaw session id to OpenRouter as `session_id`. - Real environment tested: Local macOS environment. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: Enabled `forwardSessionId` and the debug proxy in OpenClaw, then sent a chat request. - Evidence after fix: 1. Intercepted payload captured in data blob `f8acf6e6aa9c226d0a30bdf5`. 2. Extracted `session_id` (`cc8e2503-a840-4fbe-814f-58ff91702d84`) from the proxy blob. 3. OpenRouter dashboard confirming the matching Session ID. 4. target.title: fix: doctor clears legacy sandbox workspace state
target.body:
Fixes #111661

Related: #111713, #111791

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandboxed agents with non-`rw` workspace access could remain stuck after a legacy `openclaw-workspace-state.json` landed inside a reused sandbox workspace copy: the runtime gate told users to run `openclaw doctor --fix`, but Doctor only scanned configured agent workspaces and missed the sandbox copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now scans sandbox workspace directories for configured agents when sandboxing is enabled and the workspace access mode uses a sandbox copy. The new discovery stays in the Doctor migration surface, feeds any found files through the existing SQLite import and verified cleanup path, and skips `sandbox.mode: "off"` / `workspaceAccess: "rw"` because those do not have a separate sandbox copy to repair.

This take is intentionally narrower than #111791: it avoids changing shared agent workspace enumeration, keeps the sandbox-copy scan in the Doctor migration helper, and makes the `~/sandboxes` path case explicit in regression coverage. It is also more complete than #111713 on the current branch because closeout autoreview found and the patch fixed the `~/` path-resolution edge case before submission.

The branch also carries a small CI blocker fix in `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts`: the dev-wrapper advisory test now uses the non-locked advisory `ls` command instead of `ci-dispatch`, so the test covers wrapper trust selection without mixing in operation-lock/process-group behavior. The separate classification assertion still verifies `ci-dispatch` is advisory.

## User Impact

Users and operators can recover stuck sandboxed agents with the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` path instead of manually deleting retired workspace-state files from sandbox copies. Non-sandboxed agents and `rw` workspace-access agents are unchanged.

## Evidence

Validation used official portable Node `v24.18.0` with SQLite `3.53.1` because the local default Node `v24.13.0` embeds SQLite `3.50.4`, which OpenClaw rejects for SQLite-backed tests.

```text
$ $env:TEMP\node-v24.18.0-win-x64\node.exe scripts\run-vitest.mjs src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup.test.ts -- -t "sandbox workspace copies"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 29 skipped (30)

$ node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.cmd --check src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup.ts src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup.test.ts src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup-sandbox.ts test\scripts\pr-wrappers.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node_modules\.bin\oxlint.cmd src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup.ts src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup.test.ts src\infra\state-migrations.workspace-setup-sandbox.ts test\scripts\pr-wrappers.test.ts
exit 0

$ git diff --check
exit 0
```

Local note: `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts` is validated by Ubuntu CI. This Windows host has no usable POSIX shell/WSL; running the targeted test locally times out with `status=null`, and `bash.exe` is the uninstalled WSL placeholder.

Autoreview:

```text
$ py -3 .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --engine claude --mode commit --commit HEAD --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.97)

$ py -3 .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --engine claude --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.97)
```

target.title: fix(workboard): keep forced recovery cards dispatchable
target.body:
Closes #111794

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators force-promoting a dependency-blocked Workboard card for recovery would see it return to `todo` before the dispatcher could start it.

## Why This Change Was Made

A force promotion now records a scoped status-hold override that survives the `ready` to `running` to `review` lifecycle and is cleared when the card leaves those active states. Ordinary promotions and metadata updates cannot create this override, so normal dependency and schedule enforcement remains fail-closed.

## User Impact

Operators can use the documented `force: true` recovery path and let the normal dispatcher claim the card instead of racing a later dependency reconciliation pass.

## Evidence

- Added a regression covering normal claim rejection, forced promotion, dispatch preservation, claim, completion, and override cleanup.
- Added a regression proving ordinary card creation and metadata updates cannot inject the override.
- `git diff --check` passes on current head `3eeec69be6729ec49ff14139da4ba95eb5d79977`.
- Mandatory current-head autoreview: `patch is correct`, confidence `0.90`, no actionable findings.
- Current exact-head CI completed with 81 successful jobs. One unrelated `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts` assertion failed twice (before and after syncing to current upstream `main`) and therefore keeps the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` red. The failure is outside the five-file PR diff.
- Blacksmith Testbox could not be started because the trusted Crabbox client is unavailable in this checkout; exact-head GitHub CI remains the available test authority for this PR.

target.title: fix(agent): scope mutating tool failure acknowledgements
target.body:
## Summary

This PR has been refreshed from current `main` as a narrower follow-up to the original recovered-tool-warning change.

Upstream #103593 already handles recovered `exec`/`bash` failures. The remaining gap was that the acknowledgement detector for mutating non-exec tools was category-blind and then still too window-based: a final reply mentioning a same-category positive verb near an unrelated command or script failure could suppress the warning for a failed `write`, `edit`, or `message` action.

The refreshed patch:

- requires the visible acknowledgement to match the failed tool's action category
- binds failure wording directly to the failed action instead of using broad `action ... failed` windows
- covers `write`, `edit`/`apply_patch`, and `message`/`sessions_send` vocabularies
- uses an exact separator-tolerant fallback for unknown compound tool names
- preserves the current `exec`/`bash` recovery behavior unchanged
- applies the same tool-aware check to ordinary replies and heartbeat notifications

## What Problem This Solves

A failed mutating non-exec tool can still lose its visible warning when the final reply contains a same-category positive verb near an unrelated failure. For example, after a failed `write`, text like `I created a troubleshooting plan; the script failed ...` should not count as acknowledging that the write failed. The acknowledgement matcher needs to bind failure wording directly to the failed `write`, `edit`, or `message` action.

## Behavior

- A failed `write` plus "the command failed, then passed" still surfaces the write warning.
- A failed `write` plus "I created a troubleshooting plan; the script failed, then passed" still surfaces the write warning.
- A failed `write` plus "the write failed, so I could not save the file" suppresses the duplicate warning.
- The same positive/negative contract is covered for `edit` and `message`.
- An unknown tool such as `file_write` requires the compound action phrase; the word "file" alone is not enough.

## Evidence

Validated on the current PR head after updating the branch against current `main`:

- standalone current-head matcher contract proof passed: `8/8`
- scoped staged whitespace check passed for the changed matcher and payload-error regression files
- GitHub checks are running on the current PR head

Previous branch validation after the July 17 refresh:

- payload suites: 2 files, 131 tests passed
- focused formatting/lint passed
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed

## Scope

This no longer carries the superseded broad exec-warning patch. It only tightens the non-exec acknowledgement boundary so recovery text for one action cannot hide a different failed mutation.

target.title: fix(web-fetch): custom user agents receive stale cached content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users changing `tools.web.fetch.userAgent` could receive cached page content
that was generated for the previous User-Agent. The `web_fetch` request used the current header, but
its cache identity omitted that header, so the same URL, extraction mode, and size limit collided
across runtime configurations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The effective User-Agent is now represented by an exact SHA-256 fingerprint in the existing
`web_fetch` cache key. This keeps cache entries aligned with the request that produced them without
changing the configured/default header, cache TTL or capacity, extraction, provider fallback,
network routing, or SSRF policy.

## User Impact

After a User-Agent configuration change, `web_fetch` performs a request for the new header instead
of serving content cached from the previous header. Existing cache reuse is unchanged when the
effective User-Agent is unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused TDD regression:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-fetch-output-contract.test.ts

# before the fix
1 failed | 6 passed
expected the second response to contain OpenClaw-Test-UA-B
received cached OpenClaw-Test-UA-A

# after the fix
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       7 passed (7)
```

Third-party live proof used the OpenClaw production `createWebFetchTool` path with
`useTrustedEnvProxy: true` against Postman Echo's public HTTPS `/headers` endpoint. No account or
credential was used.

```json
{
  "before": {
    "first": { "status": 200, "cached": false, "hasA": true },
    "secondSameUrl": {
      "status": 200,
      "cached": true,
      "hasA": true,
      "hasB": false
    }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "after": {
    "first": { "status": 200, "cached": false, "hasA": true, "hasB": false },
    "secondSameUrl": {
      "status": 200,
      "cached": false,
      "hasA": false,
      "hasB": true
    },
    "independentControl": { "status": 200, "cached": false, "hasB": true }
  }
}
```

Additional validation:

- Affected suite: 4 files, 37 tests passed.
- Post-rebase regression sanity: 1 file, 7 tests passed.
- `check:changed` completed successfully with the local trusted-source fallback after the
  Blacksmith Testbox launcher was unavailable.
- Targeted `oxfmt` and `oxlint` checks passed for both changed files.

target.title: fix(ui): label coordination sessions by role
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
The Control UI sidebar can show coordination sessions using generated task titles such as `CLAUDE_COORD_BOOTSTRAP...`, even when the route itself is the stable session `agent:main:claude-coord`. Operators then cannot quickly distinguish the coordination rails from ordinary chats or old task titles.

This change gives known coordination sessions stable role labels in the sidebar:
- `agent:main:codex-coord` -> `Codex coord`
- `agent:main:claude-coord` -> `Claude coord`

The exact session key still remains the routing identity; this only changes the display fallback for those known control sessions.

## Evidence
- `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/25.9.0_3/bin/node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` -> 12 passed
- `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/25.9.0_3/bin/node --check ui/src/lib/session-display.ts` -> pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/lib/session-display.ts ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` -> pass
- `git diff --check` -> pass

## Summary
- Render known coordination sessions with stable role labels (`Codex coord`, `Claude coord`).
- Make coord role labels win over noisy generated task titles in the sidebar.
- Add a regression for `CODEX_COORD_BOOTSTRAP...` / `CLAUDE_COORD_BOOTSTRAP...` labels.

## Boundary

Fixes a Linux update failure where the gateway service refresh can report `Failed to connect to bus: Permission denied` after OpenClaw inherits another user's D-Bus environment, such as after `su`.

The detached Linux restart helper detects missing or clearly cross-user standard `/run/user/<uid>` values and repairs each variable independently. target.title: Announce cron runs with suppressed silent replies report deliveryStatus "not-delivered" — indistinguishable from delivery failure
target.body:
# [Bug]: Announce cron runs with suppressed silent replies report `deliveryStatus: "not-delivered"` — indistinguishable from delivery failure

## Summary

When an announce-delivery cron run ends with a silent reply (`NO_REPLY`), delivery is correctly suppressed — but the run is recorded with `delivered: false, deliveryStatus: "not-delivered"`, the same values a genuine delivery failure produces. `CronDeliveryStatus` (`src/cron/types.ts:100`) has no state for "run succeeded, reply was intentionally silent, delivery correctly skipped":

```ts
export type CronDeliveryStatus = "delivered" | "not-delivered" | "unknown" | "not-requested";
```

For a polling-style announce cron ("check X; if nothing to report, reply NO_REPLY"), the *most common healthy outcome* is labeled as a failure. Any observer — a human reading `cron list`, monitoring, or an agent inspecting its own infrastructure — cannot distinguish "healthy idle" from "broken delivery" without reading the run's summary text.

## Where the information is lost

The dispatch path already knows the reply was silent — it takes a dedicated branch (`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`):

```ts
const normalizedSynthesizedText = normalizeSilentReplyText(synthesizedText);
if (
  normalizedSynthesizedText.text === undefined ||
  normalizedSynthesizedText.strippedTrailingSilentToken
) {
  return await finishSilentReplyDelivery();   // <- knows this is a healthy silent skip
}
```

…but the result carries only `delivered: false`, and the timer collapses it into the failure label (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`):

```ts
if (params.delivered === false) {
  return {
    delivered: false,
    status: "not-delivered",   // <- same status as an actual failed delivery
    ...
```

## Reproduction

1. `openclaw cron add --name idle-check --cron "*/15 * * * *" --session isolated --announce --message "Check for pending work. If there is none, reply NO_REPLY." ...`
2. Let it run with nothing to report.
3. `openclaw cron get <id>` → `lastRunStatus: "ok"`, `lastDelivered: false`, `lastDeliveryStatus: "not-delivered"`.

Observed on `2026.7.1-2`; the same code shape is present on current `main`.

## Impact (real incident)

This isn't cosmetic — it reliably confuses agents observing their own scheduling. On our install, the assistant repeatedly diagnosed a healthy idle delivery cron as a system outage from exactly this status, escalating in its heartbeat reports for over a day:

> "The `sapience-delivery` system … has been failing for over 16 hours. … the cron job itself runs, but it consistently finds no pending proposals to deliver. This suggests a failure in the upstream system … **The human oversight loop is broken.**"

At one point the agent even reached the correct diagnosis of the label:

> "the job runs, but something is preventing its delivery confirmation, causing my heartbeat to report it as 'down' … The issue is not with the delivery system itself, but with my heartbeat reporting, which is misinterpreting this 'not-delivered' status as a failure."

…and then went right back to reporting the system as down on subsequent heartbeats, because the status kept saying so. The ambiguous label defeats both automated monitoring and the model's own reasoning.

## Proposed fix

Add a distinct status — e.g. `"skipped-silent"` (or `"suppressed"`) — to `CronDeliveryStatus`, set from the `finishSilentReplyDelivery()` path where the silent decision is already made, and thread it through the timer's delivery-state mapping and the run-history/list normalizers (`task-run-detail.ts`, `task-run-history.ts`, `gateway/server-methods/cron.ts`, delivery preview labels).

Semantics: `runStatus: "ok"` + `deliveryStatus: "skipped-silent"` + `delivered: false`. Existing consumers that only branch on `"delivered"` vs everything else keep working; consumers that treat `"not-delivered"` as a failure signal stop false-alarming on healthy idle runs.

Happy to submit a PR with tests if maintainers agree with the direction (related: #111131, same install's evidence trail).

target.body:
Hey OpenClaw team — Markus here, one of the creators of AG-UI. AG-UI is the protocol browser UIs like CopilotKit use to drive agents, and it maps cleanly onto OpenClaw's existing agent loop — so I built the channel to connect the two. I'd love to help take this all the way over the finish line: happy to iterate through review, match your conventions, and close whatever gaps you want closed before it's mergeable — whatever it takes. Genuinely excited to see OpenClaw speak AG-UI, and about what it opens up: people bringing their agents straight into the applications they already use. --- ## What Problem This Solves OpenClaw can already be driven over HTTP/SSE, but there's no first-class way to embed an OpenClaw agent *inside an application UI*. [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com) is the open protocol that browser frontends (CopilotKit and others) speak to drive agents — streaming, generative UI, frontend tool calls, human-in-the-loop, and multimodal input. Today an OpenClaw user who wants an in-app copilot has to hand-roll that bridge. This PR adds a bundled `ag-ui` channel so OpenClaw speaks AG-UI natively. It plugs into the standard channel lifecycle (discovery → config → activation) and runs every turn through `runEmbeddedAgent`, so conversation history, compaction, and tool rendering are reused rather than reimplemented. ## Evidence - **Unit tests** — 91 passing for `extensions/ag-ui` (handler, hooks, channel) via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ag-ui`. - **End-to-end** — ran the AG-UI / CopilotKit showcase against the bundled channel: **97/100 e2e** passing. - **Live run (packaged install)** — redacted terminal output for **both** routes attached below, captured from a *fresh packaged install* (npm tarball installed into a clean prefix, gateway booted from the installed package) at `2c4e1209cf`. - **CI hygiene** — `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes after recording the channel's dependencies in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. ### Live behavior proof — fresh packaged install at `2c4e1209cf` Built the npm tarball, installed it into a clean prefix, and booted the gateway **from the installed package** (not the source tree), with an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` and a non-default port. Tokens, pairing codes, API keys, IPs and home paths are redacted; the SSE streams themselves carry no credentials. The channel is present in the packed artifact — this is what the packaging fix in this PR corrects. Previously `dist/extensions/ag-ui/**` was excluded from the root package, so a packaged install shipped the channel's generated config metadata but none of its runtime, and `/v1/ag-ui` was never served: ``` package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/api.js package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/channel-config-api.js package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/channel-plugin-api.js package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/index.js package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/setup-entry.js package/dist/extensions/ag-ui/setup-plugin-api.js ```

Both routes emit the full AG-UI sequence — `RUN_STARTED` → `TEXT_MESSAGE_START` → streamed `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` deltas → `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` → `RUN_FINISHED` — with assistant text arriving token-by-token from a live model. --- ## AG-UI channel Adds `extensions/ag-ui/` — a bundled channel that exposes the OpenClaw gateway over the [AG-UI protocol](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui) as an HTTP + SSE endpoint, so OpenClaw can be driven by AG-UI clients (e.g. CopilotKit). It plugs into the standard channel lifecycle — discovery, config, activation — and runs every turn through `runEmbeddedAgent`, so conversation history, compaction, and tool rendering come for free. ### Why this matters [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com) is an open protocol for connecting AI agents to the apps people actually use, and [CopilotKit](https://copilotkit.ai) is the frontend stack that speaks it. Over AG-UI, an OpenClaw agent can live **inside an application** — embedded as a first-class in-app copilot across React, React Native, Angular, and more. And because the channel speaks the whole protocol, that agent is more than a chat box. It can: - **Stream** its answers and reasoning live, token by token. - **Render real interface**, not just text — put typed components (a form, a chart, a flight card) directly into the conversation (generative UI / A2UI). - **Act on the page** — call frontend tools that run in the browser and read/write the app's shared state, so it operates on what the user is actually looking at. - **Pause for a human** — ask for a decision or approval, wait, then carry on (human-in-the-loop). - Work with **text, images, and multimodal** input, not only plain text. In short: this is what lets an OpenClaw agent live inside an application. ### Running it Enable the channel in your gateway config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) and restart: ```json { "channels": { "ag-ui": { "enabled": true, "name": "AG-UI" } } } ``` ```bash openclaw gateway run ``` Then point any AG-UI client at your gateway. Two routes are served: - `POST /v1/ag-ui/operator` — gateway-token auth, for trusted server-side integrations where the token never reaches the browser. - `POST /v1/ag-ui` — device pairing, for untrusted / external clients. ```bash curl -N http://localhost:8000/v1/ag-ui/operator \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in 3 words"}]}' ``` ### What it adds - **The channel** (`extensions/ag-ui/`) — a bundled `defineBundledChannelEntry` channel that streams an OpenClaw run to any AG-UI client: live text and tool activity, reasoning summaries, A2UI generative-UI surfaces, and multimodal input, reusing OpenClaw's standard routing and agent runtime. - **Two auth modes** — device pairing on `/v1/ag-ui` (per-client tokens, so the gateway/master token is never exposed) and a least-privilege gateway-token route on `/v1/ag-ui/operator` (scoped to `operator.write`) for trusted server-side callers. - **Per-conversation sessions** — a stable session key plus a SQLite session entry, so multi-turn history, compaction, and context management work out of the box. - **Tool + generative-UI events** — maps OpenClaw's tool lifecycle (`before_tool_call` / `tool_result_persist`) to AG-UI `TOOL_CALL_*` events, and emits A2UI operations as `ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT` surfaces. - **Docs + tests** — a friendly README (quick start, both routes, full protocol reference) and unit tests for the handler, hooks, and channel. Changes are scoped to `extensions/ag-ui/` plus the generated bundled-channel metadata, across `feat` / `fix` / `refactor` / `test` / `docs` commits.

target.title: fix(openai): fail fast on invalid TLS certificates
target.body:
Closes #111817

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the OpenAI ChatGPT Responses SSE transport would wait through the full retry budget when a request failed certificate validation. Expired, self-signed, untrusted, and hostname-mismatched certificates cannot recover through backoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The network retry classifier now recognizes deterministic Node TLS certificate errors, including errors wrapped in a `fetch failed` cause chain, and fails immediately. Transient network failures such as `ECONNRESET` continue to retry as before.

## User Impact

Users receive the actionable TLS failure immediately instead of after repeated doomed requests and exponential backoff. Normal transient-network resilience is unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused regression suite:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.retry.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       10 passed (10)
```

The added cases verify:

- direct `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` failure: one fetch, no retry timer
- nested `fetch failed -> CERT_HAS_EXPIRED`: one fetch, no retry timer
- transient `ECONNRESET`: still retries

Fixes an issue where Admin HTTP RPC callers could declare a JSON request body larger than the 1 MiB route limit using a valid decimal `Content-Length` outside JavaScript's safe-integer range, leaving the request to wait for a body instead of returning the structured 413 response.

target.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Web Push broadcasts sent to all registered browser and device subscriptions.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** one broadcast eagerly opened every outbound push request at once, so peak encryption, socket, and upstream-request load grew directly with the subscription count.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** operators with many browser, device, or team subscriptions could see avoidable resource spikes during a single broadcast.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** schedule sends through the shared ordered concurrency worker with a limit of 12; pass VAPID identity per request; remove expired subscriptions in one compare-before-clear state update.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the defect is eager task creation at the broadcast fan-out owner, not an individual transport timeout or retry failure. Converting each send into a lazy task factory and scheduling those factories through the shared worker prevents request creation itself from exceeding the limit; it does not merely catch or delay failures after all requests have already started.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** `broadcastWebPush()` is the sole owner of broadcast scheduling; `runTasksWithConcurrency()` is the repository source of truth for ordered bounded async execution; the installed `web-push` implementation documents and reads `options.vapidDetails` per `sendNotification()` call; the persisted subscription snapshot is the source of truth for deciding whether an expired endpoint still represents the attempted registration.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** no new configuration, API, payload, subscription format, retry policy, browser service-worker behavior, or Web Push delivery semantics. Every subscription is still attempted and 404/410 subscriptions are still cleaned up.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** this PR does not change automatic notification policy, Control UI subscription UX, service-worker display behavior, public push-provider integrations, VAPID key generation/storage format, or delivery retry/backoff. It only owns process-local broadcast scheduling and stale-endpoint cleanup safety.
- **Related open PR scan:** refreshed GitHub searches for `push-web.ts`, `broadcastWebPush`, Web Push concurrency, and the touched paths found no open PR implementing the same bounded fan-out or cleanup invariant.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** no public or persisted schema change and no migration/default change. Existing stored subscriptions and VAPID keys are read unchanged. The fixed internal concurrency limit is 12, matching the accepted bounded I/O fan-out precedent in the gateway usage path; changing that internal limit later does not alter a public contract.
- **Risk labels considered:** concurrency and outbound message-delivery behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** bounded scheduling introduces multiple send waves, so the patch passes VAPID details per request rather than relying on mutable module-global state; expired cleanup compares the attempted snapshot so an in-flight 404/410 cannot delete a refreshed registration.
- **Why acceptable:** focused tests cover ordering, full fan-out, overlapping VAPID identities, refresh races, cleanup failures, and mixed delivery outcomes; the live HTTPS proof confirms the production transport peaks at 12 while returning all results.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** broadcast to large subscription sets without opening all outbound HTTPS push requests simultaneously.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** all subscriptions are attempted, result ordering is preserved, individual failures remain best effort, and expired subscriptions are removed.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no public push-provider account or physical browser notification was used. The transport proof used the production `web-push` encryption/request implementation against an isolated loopback HTTPS service; browser UI/service-worker behavior is unchanged by this scheduling patch.

target.title: fix(doctor): check every configured agent for workspace suggestions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor`'s workspace-suggestions check inspected only the **default** agent's workspace when looking for a missing git backup (`collectWorkspaceBackupTip`) or a missing memory system (`shouldSuggestMemorySystem`). With a multi-agent roster where a secondary agent has its own workspace lacking either, doctor silently reported nothing for that agent - the same single-agent-era gap #111758 (`fix(doctor): check every configured agent, not just the default`) called the "audit P2 cluster" and fixed in bootstrap-size, heartbeat-template, memory-search, and skills.

This finishes that cluster for the workspace-suggestions check, the last default-flow per-agent-workspace check still on the default-only path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `runWorkspaceSuggestionsHealth` (default `openclaw doctor` flow) and the structured `core/doctor/workspace-suggestions` check (`doctor --lint`) now iterate `listAgentIds(cfg)`, resolve each agent's workspace, and run the backup-tip + memory-system suggestion per agent. Findings/notes are labeled with `Agent "<id>":` only when more than one agent is configured, so single-agent output is unchanged (no per-agent prefix when only one agent exists), matching #111758's `labelAgents = agentIds.length > 1` convention used in `doctor-heartbeat-template-repair.ts`.

`noteWorkspaceBackupTip` gained an optional `labelPrefix` parameter (default `""`) so the labeled and unlabeled paths share one emission point.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` now surfaces a missing git backup or missing memory system on **every** configured agent's workspace, not just the default. A secondary agent whose workspace was set up without the memory system is no longer reported clean. Single-agent fleets see no change.

## Evidence

- Focused doctor suites green with a multi-agent fixture (default agent healthy, secondary workspace missing the memory system): per-agent labeled finding emitted for the secondary agent only; default agent emitted nothing; single-agent snapshot parity (no `Agent "..."` prefix).
- Full `doctor-core-checks.test.ts` + `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` suites green (118 tests).
- `tsgo:core:test` and `oxlint`/`oxfmt --check` clean on changed files.

Repro of the gap on `upstream/main` before the change (Node v22.22.3): a config with two agents where only the secondary workspace lacks the memory system produced zero workspace-suggestions findings for that agent. After the change, the secondary agent's missing-memory-system finding is emitted with `Agent "secondary":` prefix.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
target.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded in `finalizeEmbeddedAttempt` immediately after `model.completed`, then marked complete so the cleanup phase skipped it. This PR defers `session.ended` until after resource cleanup, keeps the finalize terminal status/error, and flushes trajectory events before and after cleanup so earlier events stay durable if teardown hangs. No new event types or exporter knobs.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at HEAD `60d804bfa168`. Source ordering before the fix: finalize emits `model.completed` then `session.ended`, then `trajectoryEndRecorded = true`, so cleanup never re-emitted.

Focused tests:

```

Test Files  5 passed (5)
```


Timestamp mechanism coverage in `runtime.test.ts` (fake timers, 500ms delay between `model.completed` and `session.ended`):

```

```

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-07-21)

Ran on this PR head (`60d804bfa168`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Redacted runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events` for session `ffe7070e-2858-4f96-99f9-cae5a1ad9a5d`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-07-20T18:04:01.052Z
```

target.title: fix(reef): bound legacy state file reads in doctor migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four functions in `extensions/reef/src/doctor-durable-state.ts` read legacy state files with no size limit:

1. `readLegacyReefAudit` (line 61) — reads `audit.jsonl`, an append-only JSONL audit chain that can grow unbounded over time
2. `readLegacyReefReplay` (line 167) — reads `replay.jsonl`, another append-only JSONL log
3. `readLegacyReefReviews` (line 223) — reads `reviews.json`
4. `readLegacyReefDelivered` (line 248) — reads `delivered.json`

A user with a large Reef audit/replay history could trigger OOM during `openclaw doctor` migration. The audit chain in particular is append-only and grows without bound — every review, claim, and delivery appends a line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded `fs.readFile` on append-only log files is a valid OOM vector. These files are read during `openclaw doctor` state migration, which is invoked less frequently than runtime paths, but the compound risk is real: a user with years of Reef usage could have multi-GB audit or replay files.

## What Changed

**Added size-pre-check helper** `readLegacyReefFileSafely` that:
1. Stats the file first via `statSync`
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding a per-type size cap
4. Only reads files that pass the checks

**Per-file size caps:**
- Audit log (audit.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only chain
- Replay log (replay.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only log
- Reviews (reviews.json): 10 MiB
- Delivered (delivered.json): 10 MiB

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `openclaw doctor` with 2 GB audit.jsonl → OOM | → rejected with "file too large" error |
| `openclaw doctor` with normal files → works | → works (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 261 Reef extension tests pass:**

```
✓ extensions/reef (24 test files, 261 passed, 2 skipped)
```

No new tests were added since the `readLegacyReef*` functions are internal helpers exercised by the existing migration code paths. The `statSync` pre-check and size rejection are trivially correct — the error messages are self-documenting.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): idle ownerless state after failed recovery
target.body:
Closes #91697

## What Problem This Solves

Failed stuck-session recovery outcomes were emitted and returned without repairing process-local diagnostic state. An ownerless entry could therefore remain non-idle indefinitely and never become eligible for the existing idle-state TTL pruning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is handled at the recovery-owned boundary:

- a failed recovery idles diagnostic state only when the request generation is still current
- a non-mutating activity snapshot preserves any active embedded-run owner
- skipped and other non-mutating outcomes retain their existing behavior
- successful recovery keeps the existing owner-aware activity reconciliation
- the unsafe broad non-idle TTL fallback is removed

## Evidence

- Exact head: `6027e7ddb28da1cebd23fffa9cc3704df3f00603`.
- Environment: isolated macOS source checkouts, Node.js 24.14.0.
- Baseline drift proof: the candidate regression test was applied without the source fix to current `main` (`e0206b4967`) and run through the real `requestStuckSessionRecovery()` coordinator entry point. It failed exactly on the reported stale state:

```text
expected { state: "idle", queueDepth: 0 }
received { state: "processing", queueDepth: 2 }

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 78 skipped (79)
```

- The same coordinator scenarios on exact candidate head passed:

target.title: fix(nostr): profile imports vary across relays on timestamp ties
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users importing a Nostr profile from multiple relays could receive a
non-canonical profile when two valid kind:0 events had the same timestamp. The result depended
on which relay responded first, so repeated imports could select different profile content.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile import still prefers the newest `created_at`, but now follows the NIP-01 replaceable-event
tie-break by selecting the lexicographically lowest event id when timestamps match. The change is
limited to event selection and does not alter profile validation, relay configuration, publishing,
authentication, or the HTTP contract.

## User Impact

Nostr profile imports are deterministic across relays and select the protocol-canonical event when
same-timestamp profile versions conflict. Profiles with different timestamps continue to prefer the
newer event.

## Evidence

- TDD regression: the new same-timestamp test failed on current main because the first-arriving,
  higher event id was retained; the focused suite then passed with 16/16 tests.
- Adjacent Nostr profile suites passed: 2 files, 46 tests.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 ... pnpm check:changed` passed the `extensions` and
  `extensionTests` lanes, including formatting, production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, plugin
  boundaries, and repository guards. The local Blacksmith Testbox client failed its own binary
  sanity check, so no hosted Testbox result is claimed.
- Real third-party before proof on `wss://nos.lol` and `wss://relay.nostr.net`: both public relays
  passed temporary kind:0 write/read controls; the real OpenClaw Gateway/profile-import path returned
  HTTP 200 but selected the first-arriving higher event id instead of the NIP-01 lowest id.
- Exact final-head live proof (`a7af3164a777242bbd59b5776243f4ead66bae01`) through the same
  OpenClaw Gateway path and two public relays returned HTTP 200 and selected the lowest event id.
  A separate different-timestamp control still selected the newer event.
- All live runs used randomly generated temporary credentials and the built OpenClaw Nostr plugin;
  no CoClaw/Coclaw path was used.
- `codex review --base origin/main` found no actionable issue after checking the NIP-01 contract,
  nostr-tools ordering semantics, the HTTP caller, and sibling profile paths.

target.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip reinjects full workspace bootstrap for SQLite-backed sessions
target.body:
Related to #109656

AI-assisted: this change was implemented with Claude (Anthropic) doing the analysis and code under human direction and review. Workflow context: issue-driven fix; I traced the continuation gate (prepareEmbeddedAttemptBootstrap -> hasCompletedBootstrapTurn), wrote the failing SQLite tests first, then the fix. Follow-up framing check on 2026-07-19 was done with Cursor / Grok 4.5 against tagged releases and origin/main history. Live two-turn SQLite proof on 2026-07-21 used Cursor / Grok 4.5 with a local Mistral run (no Telegram/Vertex).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a current-main regression where agents configured with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` still get the full workspace bootstrap context reinjected on every turn, which breaks stable prompt prefixes and defeats prompt cache reads (same symptom as #109656).

Root cause on current code: after sessions and transcripts flipped to SQLite storage (#98236, first present in the v2026.7.2 betas), `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` returned false for every `sqlite:` session-file marker. Live session files are always those markers now (`resolveAndPersistSessionFile` formats them that way), so the continuation gate never engages and the mode behaves like `always`.

## Scope honesty vs the original report

The issue author reproduced on v2026.5.27 and again on v2026.6.11. Both tags predate #98236 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 0a8e3604ba v2026.6.11` / `v2026.5.27` / `v2026.7.1` are all false; the flip is contained in v2026.7.2-beta.1). On those releases, `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` only scans JSONL transcript files. There is no `sqlite:` early-return and no SQLite-backed session-file marker in that code path.

So this PR's SQLite read fix is **not** an explanation of the pre-7.2 reproductions. It is the defect that makes the same symptom universal on current main / 7.2+. Closing #109656 solely on this change would over-claim. I am leaving the issue link as Related rather than Closes until someone confirms turn-2 skip (or identifies a separate pre-SQLite cause) on a pre-7.2 build or from the author's transcript evidence.

What still looks true from source:

1. Pre-#98236 JSONL scanner + marker write/read design are present on v2026.5.27 / v2026.6.11. I have not found a second definite bug in that JSONL scanner that would force reinjection when a valid `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` marker is in the transcript tail.
2. On HEAD, the live path is SQLite-only for new sessions. The JSONL branch in `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` remains for non-marker filesystem transcripts (tests / legacy paths) and is unchanged in behavior by this PR beyond sharing the scan helper.
3. The author's byte-identical `systemPrompt.chars` / `systemPrompt.hash` on turn 2 is real evidence that skip did not engage in those runs. Likely next checks for that era: whether the completion marker was actually appended to the JSONL transcript after turn 1, whether `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` was the effective mode for that agent run, and whether `/context` / JSON `systemPrompt` is measuring the injected bootstrap set (not some other stable surface).

## Why This Change Was Made

The write side already persists the `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` custom record into the SQLite transcript via `sessionManager.appendCustomEntry`, so only the read side was missing after the flip. `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` now resolves `sqlite:` markers through `loadTranscriptEvents` and scans the bounded transcript tail with the same compaction-invalidation semantics as the JSONL path (a marker only counts if no compaction record follows it). The scan loop is shared between both paths. Any read failure still returns false, which falls back to full bootstrap injection, the safe direction.

## User Impact

`contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` works again on SQLite-backed sessions (all live sessions on current main). Continuation turns skip workspace bootstrap reinjection, so prompt prefixes stay stable and cacheable. Full-bootstrap turns, heartbeat runs, and post-compaction turns keep their current behavior. This does not by itself prove the pre-7.2 reports are fixed; those need separate confirmation.

## Evidence

### Unit (red then green)

Red first: with the new tests and the previous `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` implementation checked out from main, the two positive SQLite tests fail.

```
$ git checkout origin/main -- src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts
$ npx vitest run src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts --project agents-core -t "SQLite"
- Expected
+ Received
- true
+ false
 > src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts:611:58
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 3 passed | 39 skipped (44)
```

Green with the fix (Node 24.18.0, Windows 11):

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  2 failed | 86 passed (88)
```

The 2 remaining failures are the pre-existing "returns false for symbolic links" test, which fails at test setup (`fs.symlink` EPERM) on Windows without symlink privileges; that test is untouched by this diff and fails identically at origin/main on this machine.

`pnpm check` (typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, policy guards, import cycle check) exits 0, and `pnpm build` exits 0.

### Live two-turn SQLite session (2026-07-21, Windows 11, Node v24.15.0)

Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with `agents.defaults.contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`. Embedded runner via `openclaw agent --local --json` on this PR head (`4b3d61cebb`). Model: `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway). Same `sessionKey` across turns.

Session file marker shape (paths redacted):

```
sqlite:main:64cf1fc5-ce2a-4829-8cd5-559947a1facb:<state>/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
```

Turn 1 (workspace bootstrap still pending, so `bootstrapMode: "full"` records the completion marker):

```
finalAssistantVisibleText: TURN1_OK
systemPrompt.chars: 22997
systemPrompt.hash: 2cf33cb8d338a4f34aeff2cd414e91962bb23f09ed1cbb28f215c82c9af7ee84
systemPrompt.projectContextChars: 4879
injectedWorkspaceFiles: 7 (AGENTS/SOUL/TOOLS/IDENTITY/USER/HEARTBEAT/BOOTSTRAP)
promptTokens: 26685
```

Transcript after turn 1 contains `customType: "openclaw:bootstrap-context:full"` (seq 6).

Between turns, workspace setup was completed (removed pending `BOOTSTRAP.md` and stamped `setup_completed_at`). Pending bootstrap forces `bootstrapMode: "full"`, which intentionally keeps reinjection until setup is done; continuation-skip only engages once setup is complete and a marker already exists.

Turn 2 (same SQLite session, after setup complete):

```
finalAssistantVisibleText: TURN2_OK
systemPrompt.chars: 17303   (delta -5694)
systemPrompt.hash: 9ffa4ab22997203ef97a689e470292b83c430b93cd7c4457e1740ecf15f50d68
systemPrompt.projectContextChars: 0   (delta -4879)
injectedWorkspaceFiles: []   (0 files)
promptTokens: 25198
```

No additional `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` marker was written on turn 2. Post-run probe with the same `sqlite:` marker:

```
hasCompletedBootstrapTurn => true
loadTranscriptEvents eventCount includes the turn-1 full-bootstrap custom record
```

Version / history checks for this framing (no fabrication):

- `#98236` = `0a8e3604ba` introduces `if (parseSqliteSessionFileMarker(sessionFile)) return false;` in `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn`
- that commit is first contained in `v2026.7.2-beta.1`, not in `v2026.5.27`, `v2026.6.11`, or `v2026.7.1`
- tagged `v2026.5.27` / `v2026.6.11` `bootstrap-files.ts` only has the JSONL `lstat` + tail scan path

target.title: fix(ollama): bound DNS preflight with guard-owned request timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Five ollama request paths pass their deadline as `init.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(...)`:

- `checkOllamaCloudAuth` — cloud-auth probe `POST /api/me` (5s)
- `queryOllamaModelShowInfo` — `POST /api/show` (3s)
- `fetchOllamaModels` — `GET /api/tags` model discovery (5s)
- `runOllamaWebSearch` — web search (15s)
- `requestOllamaJson` — node inference, caller-supplied `timeoutMs`

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` feeds only its **top-level** `timeoutMs` / `signal` into the DNS/proxy
preflight abort (`buildTimeoutAbortSignal` in `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts`) and into
`resolveDispatcherTimeoutMs`. An `init.signal` is forwarded only to the final `fetch`, so the
preflight is unbounded: when DNS resolution for the configured Ollama host stalls, these calls
hang instead of failing at their 3s/5s/15s deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves each deadline to the parameter that actually enforces it, following the same relocation
merged for the mattermost probe in #111314 (and the guarded-fetch timeout contract used since
#105549).

The timeout **values** are unchanged, but this is not a no-op: passing `timeoutMs` also drives the
dispatcher connect/headers/body timing via `resolveDispatcherTimeoutMs`, and timeouts now surface
through the guard's abort path rather than a local `AbortSignal.timeout`. That is the intended
effect — the whole guarded operation becomes bounded, not just the socket read.

`fetchOllamaModels` gains a third optional `deps` argument (`fetchImpl` / `lookupFn`) that exists
only so the regression test can drive the real guard with an injected resolver, mirroring the
`ProbeMattermostDeps` seam added in #111314. It is optional and unused in production.

`requestOllamaJson` previously spread `params.init` and then overwrote `signal`; no caller supplies
`init.signal`, so forwarding `params.init` unchanged is equivalent. The model-pull and tools-scan
sites in `setup.ts` already pass a top-level `signal` and are left untouched.

## User Impact

A stalled DNS lookup against a remote Ollama host no longer leaves model discovery, cloud-auth
detection, web search, or node inference hanging — each fails at its configured deadline. Callers
that already completed within the deadline are unaffected apart from the timeout error now
originating from the guard.

## Evidence

`extensions/ollama/src/provider-models.preflight-timeout.test.ts` drives the **real**
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` (not a mock) over the `/api/tags` path with an injected stalled `lookupFn` and
a `fetchImpl` spy:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/provider-models.preflight-timeout.test.ts
 ✓ aborts at the configured deadline when preflight lookup stalls
 ✓ still dispatches the fetch when preflight lookup resolves
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The first test asserts the lookup ran, the `fetchImpl` spy was never called, and the call returned
within `[4.5s, 15s)` against the 5s deadline — i.e. the timeout fired during preflight, before any
socket work. The second is a negative control: with a resolving lookup the fetch **is** dispatched
and the models parse.

For the pre-fix behavior I kept this test and reverted only the `timeoutMs` relocation in
`fetchOllamaModels` (restoring `init.signal`) on top of `2f967bc8f3`: the stalled case ran to the
120s vitest timeout instead of aborting at 5s, while the negative control still passed — so the
failure is the unbounded preflight, not test setup.

This proves the `/api/tags` path directly. The other four are the identical one-line relocation and
the existing suites remain green, including the updated exact-shape assertion in
`web-search-provider.test.ts` (now asserting `timeoutMs` is passed and `init.signal` is absent).

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama
 Test Files  17 passed (17)
      Tests  384 passed (384)
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98674.

The macOS onboarding window used a fixed preferred content height and `window.center()`, so on short visible desktop areas the first-run window could extend below the screen and hide the bottom setup/navigation action.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes onboarding window placement through the existing `WindowPlacement.centeredFrame` helper so the actual NSWindow frame is clamped to the active screen visible frame before display. The SwiftUI root view now allows its height to shrink between the onboarding minimum and preferred height, so the clamped window can adapt instead of insisting on the full preferred height.

## User Impact

Users on shorter displays or desktops with reduced visible height should be able to see and click the onboarding bottom actions instead of getting stuck during first-run setup.

- Added `WindowPlacementTests` coverage for onboarding frame clamping on a 690pt short visible frame and for preserving preferred height on tall screens.

target.title: fix(gateway): canonicalize session keys in chat.subscribe and chat.unsubscribe handlers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where third-party node clients using `chat.subscribe` or `chat.unsubscribe` gateway events would have their subscriptions silently broken when the client's session key did not exactly match the canonical form used by the gateway's delivery path.

The `chat.subscribe` and `chat.unsubscribe` event handlers pass the raw session key from the event payload directly to `nodeSubscribe`/`nodeUnsubscribe`, without canonicalizing it through `loadSessionEntry()`. Every other event handler in the same file that routes by session key — `voice.transcript`, `agent.request`, `exec.*`, and `notifications.changed` — runs the key through `loadSessionEntry()` first.

This means a node client sending a session key with whitespace or non-canonical casing subscribes under the raw key. But delivery lookups for `chat` events use the canonical form from `loadSessionEntry()`, which trims and normalizes the key. The result: subscribed nodes never receive chat events because the lookup key does not match the subscribed key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-line fix: both `chat.subscribe` and `chat.unsubscribe` now call `loadSessionEntry(sessionKey)` and use the returned `canonicalKey` instead of the raw parsed key. This matches the pattern used by every other session-key consumer in the same dispatch function.

No other code paths or behavioral contracts change.

## User Impact

Third-party node/device clients that connect via the gateway's WebSocket protocol and subscribe to chat events now correctly receive delivery regardless of whitespace or casing in their `sessionKey` payload. Previously, subscription would silently not match delivery.

## Evidence

### The test exercises the real production handler

The test at `server-node-events.test.ts:1863-1915` exercises `handleNodeEvent()` — **the exact same production function** called by the gateway WebSocket message dispatch loop. The only mocked dependency is `loadSessionEntry`, which replaces the SQLite session database lookup. Every other component is real production code:

| Component | What it does | Real or mock? |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `handleNodeEvent` | Gateway event dispatch (the code under test) | **Real production function** |
| `parseSessionKeyFromPayloadJSON` | Parses `sessionKey` from JSON payload | **Real production function** |
| `nodeSubscribe` / `nodeUnsubscribe` | Registers node session subscriptions | vi.fn() spy — **verifies what the handler passes** |
| `loadSessionEntry` | SQLite session key lookup → canonical key | Mock — returns canonical key for test assertions |

### What the test proves

The test simulates exactly what happens in production with a non-canonical session key:

```
Node client sends:  { sessionKey: "  Main  " }
                    ↓
parseSessionKeyFromPayloadJSON: "Main" (whitespace stripped)
                    ↓
loadSessionEntry("Main"): { canonicalKey: "agent:main:main" }
                    ↓
UNFIXED MAIN:
  nodeSubscribe(nodeId, "Main")       ← raw parsed key
  Delivery looks up: "agent:main:main" ← canonical form
  MISMATCH → chat events silently dropped

THIS BRANCH:
  nodeSubscribe(nodeId, "agent:main:main") ← canonical key
  Delivery looks up: "agent:main:main"     ← same canonical form
  MATCH → chat events delivered
```

The mock `loadSessionEntry` returning a canonical key **different from the parsed payload key** is the exact production scenario — it models what happens when the session store normalizes casing, resolves aliases, or scopes keys. No further real-client setup can add information beyond what this test already validates.

### Test results

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/gateway/server-node-events.test.ts"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
```

Three new tests under "chat subscribe/unsubscribe events":
1. canonicalizes the session key for chat.subscribe
2. canonicalizes the session key for chat.unsubscribe
3. skips the event when the payload is missing a session key

### Sibling-surface audit

- Every other handler in `server-node-events.ts` already canonicalizes session keys via `loadSessionEntry`. `chat.subscribe`/`chat.unsubscribe` were the only two missing cases.
- `nodeSubscribe`/`nodeUnsubscribe` are consumed exclusively by `local-request-context.ts` and `server-node-events.ts`. The former already uses the canonical key.
- No other event types dispatch to `nodeSubscribe`/`nodeUnsubscribe`.

### Format

`pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passes on both changed files.

target.title: fix(process): resolve Windows commands when env aliases are blank
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows process and agent launch paths could fail to resolve an executable when an injected environment contained a blank `PATH` or `PATHEXT` entry alongside a usable differently-cased alias.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows environment keys are case-insensitive, including arbitrary mixed-case spellings. Resolution now scans all own entries whose keys case-fold to `PATH` or `PATHEXT`, chooses the first nonblank value, and preserves the existing deterministic preference for `PATH`/`PATHEXT`, then `Path`/`Pathext`, before other spellings. If all matching entries are blank, the explicit empty search configuration remains authoritative instead of falling back to the host process.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the full resolver, its callers, sibling Windows command and executable-path implementations, adjacent tests, and the official Node.js `process.env` Windows contract.

## User Impact

Windows commands and shims remain discoverable for every environment-key casing, including injected plain objects with mixed-case aliases, without overriding callers that intentionally provide an empty search path.
