target.title: fix(gateway): avoid stale wake delays after node re-pairing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where removing, revoking, rotating, reapproving, or silently superseding a disconnected paired node could leave admitted work or push ownership behind. A revoked installation could still accept work, an old generation could send APNs after its ownership changed, and a same-ID replacement could inherit stale queues or wake state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway exposed two pairing-removal APIs, but runtime cleanup was local to the node method and did not own wake lifecycle state or the explicit pending-work queue, so full device removal skipped it and in-flight or queued work could outlive the removed pairing. Silent pairing pruning deleted the same persistent state while skipping runtime and APNs cleanup entirely. The pending-work RPC also allowed whitespace-equivalent node IDs to split one logical node across a trimmed queue/APNs key and a raw wake-lifecycle key. A node-ID lifecycle alone was still insufficient because removal deletes that controller and a later request can create a fresh one for a same-ID replacement. Runtime cleanup now has one shared owner used by explicit removal and silent pruning, while asynchronous work is admitted only when the persistent record has an effective non-revoked node token and an approved node surface. The generation is derived only from node-owned identity: the device public key/creation identity, active node-role token, and node-surface approval identity. Unrelated operator approval no longer rotates node work. WebSocket and watch transports capture that generation when the paired record contains the exact signed public key and node token used for authentication, and approved sessions store it on `NodeSession`; a first node surface that is still awaiting approval remains connected without command authority until approval transitions that exact live session. Device reapproval atomically reports a node-generation transition; the Gateway invalidates node wake ownership and every node transport before approval success, disconnects them after the response flush, and revalidates every inbound WebSocket or watch RPC against the persisted generation. WebSocket connect also recaptures authenticated pairing state immediately before publishing the session. Surface reapproval uses a monotonic approval timestamp and advances the exact live session from its old generation, including the initial generation-less pending surface, to the new generation only when node ID, `connId`, the persistent generation read before approval, and the authoritative previous generation returned by the approval transaction all match, so an externally reapproved old socket cannot regain authority. Direct invocation, plugin transport dispatch, foreground actions, explicit pending queues, reconnect adoption, pull/ack, and APNs registration require the selected approved session to own the admitted generation. The production registry also rereads persistent generation immediately before every command dispatch, then rechecks invalidation, exact session generation, and `connId` after that lookup yields; filesystem, terminal, exec-approval, and Claude CLI sibling routes therefore cannot bypass the invariant. A generation mismatch rejects the operation without mutating either side because mismatch alone cannot prove whether the work or the socket is stale. Destructive pending drain completes its asynchronous persistent-generation check and exact `connId` admission before removing work, then drains and responds without yielding, so an ordinary same-generation reconnect cannot consume and lose items through the retired request. Every production wake and nudge carries both persistent currentness and its lifecycle abort signal into direct or relay APNs transport. Direct APNs revalidates ownership after session establishment and checks lifecycle cancellation immediately before the request write; relay APNs revalidates immediately before `fetch` and combines lifecycle cancellation with its timeout signal. Node-token rotation/revocation and surface approval invalidate the in-flight lifecycle, while operator-token rotation does not. Invalidated registry sessions are hidden from connected lookup and rejected again at invoke, inbound-RPC, and outbound-send boundaries. Pending enqueue captures persistent generation before wake lifecycle admission and rolls back only the exact item it created, while queues remain isolated by generation so stale pull, ack, drain, or enqueue operations cannot delete replacement work; enqueue and drain also prune expired retired-generation buckets so generation changes do not leak queue memory indefinitely. APNs event registration passes its authenticated generation into the persistence owner, which rereads paired state inside the same SQLite write transaction before writing APNs ownership. Full-device removal, device-deleting role removal, every fully deleted silent pairing, and replacement-public-key approval tombstone and delete retired APNs ownership inside the same SQLite transaction that changes pairing state. Partial node-role removal still preserves the shared registration for a surviving operator consumer, but later full pruning of that operator-only row now retires the credential. Same-key credential or surface reapproval preserves the physical installation's registration. Delayed Gateway cleanup was removed, so old ownership is cleared at the mutation boundary while a legitimate replacement registration committed afterward survives. Persistent generation checks now select only the requested `device_pairing_paired` row by its `device_id` primary key, and redundant checks across synchronous invocation sections were removed.

Chat subscription indexes now carry the authenticated pairing generation. Subscribe and unsubscribe require the exact live connection plus current persisted generation; subscribed fanout rereads persistence before a post-yield live-generation recheck. Cross-generation replacement clears inherited subscriptions, ordinary same-generation reconnect preserves them, and an exact live surface approval migrates them to the newly committed generation. Public fire-and-forget fanout also settles serialization and individual transport failures internally, so one failed subscriber cannot create an unhandled rejection or prevent the remaining subscribers from being attempted.

Surface approval now returns both its authoritative previous generation and its exact committed next generation from the same persistence transaction. Live-session promotion is allowed only across that exact transition, and a final persistent read must still equal the returned next generation; an external reapproval committed in between therefore cannot advance the old socket to an unrelated later generation. Wake lifecycle, in-flight deduplication, wake throttling, and nudge throttling are likewise owned by node ID plus pairing generation, so a replacement generation cannot inherit retired in-flight results or delays while node-wide removal still invalidates every generation.

Asynchronous `node.event` handling now freezes the exact inbound `connId` and authenticated pairing generation before the event implementation is loaded. The same currentness predicate is rechecked after every yielding stage and before session mutation, attachment or transcript persistence, receipt delivery, and agent dispatch; detached work checks again when it starts. Voice transcript replay reservations retain immutable receipt timestamps and resolve in receipt order. When each reservation reaches the front, it performs a final generation check and, without another yield, commits dedupe, starts the session-store touch, registers chat state, and invokes the agent. A rejected or newly stale event therefore cannot suppress an identical replay from the current connection, leave an orphan chat run, rebind a new session to a dropped replay, or dispatch after becoming stale while queued, while slow generation checks cannot collapse commands that arrived outside the 1.5-second replay window. This closes the case where an image-bearing `agent.request` pauses in model lookup and resumes after its node token has been revoked or replaced.

Watch invoke results now repeat exact connection-generation admission after the complete HTTP body upload and immediately before result commit. Node-targeted voice-wake trigger and routing updates use `sendEventRawForPairingGeneration` for approved sessions; command-free compatibility broadcasts remain available to the first-surface session while it has no durable generation. The generic broadcaster remains operator-only for those events and skips locally invalidated clients. Connect finalization carries authenticated pairing state through a second pre-registration check, registers approved sessions with their exact generation, and allows only the generation-less first-surface session to transition in place when approval commits. Post-handshake connection metadata is also written only when the same generation still owns the paired record; WebSocket first-connection notification scheduling then rechecks the exact live `connId` and generation.

Authenticated pairing ownership is now represented separately from approved surface authority. Every node transport carries a non-secret `pairingIdentity` derived from the paired device ID, public key, and active node token, while `pairingGeneration` remains optional until the node surface is approved. `resolveNodePairingState` returns both facts from one durable read. A first-surface session can therefore remain connected for approval and command-free compatibility delivery without being confused with a deleted or replaced pairing: registry reconciliation, node/environment inventory, active-node and Talk selection, remote skill/bin projection, inbound RPC, notifications, and delayed voice-wake snapshots all require the original identity to remain current even when no generation exists. Surface approval returns the authoritative identity from the same persistence transaction as its next generation; live promotion requires that identity, the authoritative previous generation, the final persisted state, and the exact `connId` to agree, and `NodeRegistry.updateSurface` repeats the identity guard before mutating the session.

Presence-alive metadata now follows the same ownership rule: the event passes its captured authenticated generation into a row-scoped SQLite update, which compares that generation inside the write transaction before changing `lastSeenAtMs` or `lastSeenReason`. Connected-node projections also filter the process-local registry against the pairing records already loaded for `node.list`, `node.describe`, and environment inventory, and active-node selection uses that same filtered set. Talk capability detection performs an asynchronous persistent-generation lookup; a proven mismatch invalidates the retired session, while a pairing-store read failure temporarily hides it without treating the failure as revocation.

Persistent connected-session reconciliation now freezes the exact session object, `connId`, and pairing generation before its asynchronous store lookup. If surface approval promotes that same live session while the lookup is pending, the older result is skipped instead of invalidating the newly approved generation. A proven stale generation invokes narrow runtime cleanup for the exact retired `connId`: active presence is disconnected and connection-owned remote node, bin, and node-hosted skill projections are removed, while a replacement connection's projections, queues, subscriptions, and wake state are preserved. Agent prompt construction also revalidates the published active-node generation against the persisted row at its use boundary; a mismatch or store error omits `active_node` instead of advertising a retired socket.

Remote execution eligibility, node-hosted skill construction, and scheduled bin refresh now perform synchronous persistent-generation reconciliation at their own read boundary instead of depending on an unrelated Talk request to clean process-local state. A proven mismatch invalidates the exact retired session and removes only its connection-owned projections; a store read failure hides the projection without treating it as revocation. Delayed first-connection notifications also capture the source `nodeId`, `connId`, and pairing generation when scheduled, resolve both source and targets from generation-current sessions, require the exact captured source to remain present, and revalidate a generation-bearing source immediately before each notification dispatch. A same-ID replacement must explicitly take over the pending claim; an externally rotated or silently superseded source cannot produce a false “Node connected” alert.

Remote binary inventory now uses that same canonical pairing-generation owner end to end. `NodeSession.pairingGeneration` is carried into the existing remote-node record, probe cache, and in-flight probe owner; ordinary same-generation reconnects retain their measured bins, while device/public-key, node-token, or approved-surface generation changes clear the retired inventory. `system.which` and `system.run` reuse the registry's `expectedPairingGeneration` dispatch fence, and probe results are persisted only after the existing paired-device row transaction rereads and matches that generation. Startup hydration requests an internal generation projection from `listNodePairing`, while the default `node.pair.list` result remains unchanged. This adds no parallel cache owner, cross-owner lookup, duplicate generation policy, or compatibility layer.

This branch was ported through the controlled current-main transaction required to resolve the original GitHub merge conflict, then synchronized once more onto the exact hosted CI base `7fe1d70a` because current main changed the same Gateway and infra owners. All 24 commits remain patch-identical in `git range-diff`, and the pre-repair rebased tree exactly matches hosted merge commit `d2765678`.

- **Root cause:** Pairing deletion, approval, silent pruning, token/surface/device mutation, inbound and outbound connection dispatch, chat subscription fanout, process-local lifecycle cleanup, queued work, APNs registration, presence metadata, connected-session projections, agent active-node projection, remote skill/bin caches, and delayed connection notifications had different owners. Durable role history still admitted revoked tokens; a lifecycle or subscription keyed only by node ID could be recreated or inherited after removal; an APNs authorization check or request write could outlive a generation change; a live `connId` did not prove whether the socket authenticated before or after same-ID device reapproval; an asynchronous generation lookup could observe generation A and later invalidate the same session after it had been legitimately promoted to B; an optional approved-surface generation represented both a legitimate first-surface pending session and a missing pairing row; and initial surface promotion compared only absent previous generations plus `connId`, so a retired generation-less identity could inherit its replacement's first generation. Reapproval neither retired inbound node authority nor cleared a replacement installation's APNs target; generation-wide enqueue rollback could erase successful replacement work; retired queue generations were never swept; pairing deletion committed before APNs cleanup; the shared APNs registration was treated as node-only even when a surviving operator role still consumed it; and ID-only presence writes plus process-local connected, active-node, remote-skill, scheduled-bin, and delayed-notification lookup could update, display, probe, or announce a replacement pairing through its retired socket.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Durable pairing identity is the transport-ownership source of truth for every authenticated session, approved surface generation is the narrower command/subscription authority, and exact `connId` binds both facts to one transport. Surface approval returns authoritative identity and generation from one transaction; promotion compares the captured session identity, authoritative previous generation, final persisted identity/generation, and exact connection, while the registry repeats the transition guard at the mutation boundary. Every production registry dispatch or subscribed fanout rereads persistent state immediately before send. Connected-session reconciliation binds each asynchronous result to the pre-yield object, connection, identity, and optional generation, so it cannot treat a deleted pairing as a still-valid pending surface or revoke an in-place promotion; proven invalidation removes only projections still owned by that exact retired connection. Exact surface reapproval transitions keep the one authenticated live session and its subscriptions aligned with the new persistent generation; different-identity or different-generation replacement clears that state instead of adopting it. `GatewayWsClient.invalidated` remains the immediate revocation owner only when a current persistent read independently proves the session stale, mutation owners abort active wake lifecycles, queues retain generation-local ownership, and direct/relay APNs transports enforce currentness through their final asynchronous setup and network-write boundaries. APNs registration, post-handshake node connection metadata, and presence-alive metadata reread paired generation inside their SQLite write transaction; each metadata path updates only its selected row-owned columns, so it cannot replay a stale full-table snapshot or write generation A activity into generation B. Pairing-backed inventory projections filter against their already-loaded durable pairing states, Talk capability performs a fresh persistent read, and active-node, remote execution, node-hosted skill, scheduled-bin, and connection-notification projections validate identity plus approved generation where applicable at their own use boundary. Delayed alerts retain the exact source connection and pairing state through both timer stages and revalidate it immediately before target dispatch; persistence errors fail closed without permanently invalidating a potentially valid session. Pairing deletion clears shared ownership in the same transaction only when the paired device is actually removed. The gateway revalidates these owners at their actual side-effect boundaries. Both explicit removal APIs and silent pruning clear revoked runtime ownership, while surviving mixed-role consumers retain shared APNs ownership. Ordinary socket disconnect deliberately keeps the weaker map-only cleanup because it does not revoke durable pairing identity.
- **Remote-bin owner boundary:** Binary inventory is a projection owned by the approved pairing generation, not by a reusable node ID. The existing generation resolver defines replacement, the live `NodeSession` carries that fact, the registry fences probe dispatch, and the paired-device row transaction fences persistence. Same-generation reconnect is therefore preserved without allowing a replacement generation to inherit or be overwritten by retired probe results.
- **Risk explanation:** The highest-risk area is message delivery and session-state lifecycle: invalidating too broadly could suppress a legitimate invocation after an ordinary disconnect, while invalidating too narrowly could deliver stale work to a same-ID replacement. The diff is larger because direct invocation, pending invocation, both removal APIs, the lifecycle owner, and their regression tests must move together to enforce one invariant.
- **Why acceptable:** The public gateway schema, authorization policy, storage schema, and wake/reconnect timing are unchanged. A whitespace-padded enqueue request now receives the canonical trimmed node ID in its result, and pairing-owned work stays isolated behind that identity and generation. Focused regressions cover revoked/tokenless admission, operator-only approval stability, mixed-role APNs preservation, node-token and node-surface lifecycle invalidation, direct and relay APNs ownership checks, relay lifecycle cancellation, silent-prune cleanup, invalidated raw/plugin transport, generation replacement during reconnect, non-destructive foreground and explicit queues, transactional removal/replacement ordering, guarded APNs registration, and the ordinary-disconnect distinction. The pre-port real-gateway proof still exercises the original same-ID replacement race; hosted CI remains responsible for executing the expanded exact-head suite.
- **Latest review resolution:** Deterministic interleaving tests cover exact surface-generation promotion, a generation-A lookup completing after that same session is promoted to B, independent replacement-generation wake ownership, token revocation during image-model lookup, Watch reapproval during a partial `/result` upload, external generation replacement before voice-wake update or delayed snapshot delivery, external deletion of a generation-less first-surface session, pairing-state snapshot distinction between a pending surface and a missing row, synchronous and asynchronous identity invalidation, delayed command-free snapshot revalidation, stable first-surface promotion for the same identity, external node-token rotation before first-surface approval, registry rejection of an identity-mismatched generation-less transition, shared-auth identity-only connect finalization after a pairing change, a pending stale voice transcript followed by an identical current-generation replay, two identical current events racing against an initially absent session, identical events received outside the replay window whose delayed admissions finish together, a queued replay invalidated before an earlier stale reservation releases it, a stale presence write after node-token rotation, an externally replaced connected/active session, exact-connection cleanup of remote bin and node-hosted skill projections, direct node-hosted skill construction and scheduled-bin refresh after persistent generation replacement, active-node prompt revalidation, a pairing-store read failure during synchronous or asynchronous connected-session selection, exact-source replacement during a pending alert, and source-generation rotation during the notification delay. The promoted generation remains connected and is not invalidated by the older result; a pending surface keeps its command-free connection only while its independently authenticated pairing identity remains current, and approval cannot assign a replacement identity's generation to the retired socket; shared-auth pairing changes produce the intended `NOT_PAIRED` handshake failure instead of dereferencing a missing device-token binding; the stale Watch result is rejected and its session closed; retired node transports receive no trigger or routing frame, stale voice events commit no state, only the accepted replay persists the session ID used by its dispatched command, dedupe timing remains tied to receipt rather than admission completion, queued replay admission rechecks the exact connection immediately before dispatch, the replacement pairing receives no stale last-seen update, retired sessions disappear from connected/active/Talk/prompt/remote-skill/bin-refresh projections, delayed alerts do not announce a retired source, and storage failures hide sessions without marking them revoked.

## User Impact

Operators can remove, revoke, rotate, reapprove, silently supersede, and later re-pair a mobile node without the old generation sending push, inheriting stale wake delays or chat subscriptions, receiving or pulling a command through the prior socket, acknowledging replacement-owned work, losing replacement-owned queued work, or restoring push ownership from the removed installation. An ordinary same-generation reconnect preserves its subscriptions but cannot make a stale drain delete work without delivering it. A wake invalidated before the direct request write or relay fetch is cancelled instead of being sent. Expanded surface approval remains available on the already connected node without a reconnect, including the first surface approved after a generation-less pending connection, while a socket authenticated before an unrelated external reapproval cannot be promoted and every command or subscribed-event route rejects a retired persistent generation. Expired retired-generation pending work is reclaimed. A replacement APNs registration created after removal commits is preserved, and removing only node capability from a mixed-role device keeps approval notifications working for its surviving operator role; if that surviving pairing is later fully pruned, its APNs credential is retired. Revoked or tokenless node records no longer accept new work. Operator-role or scope approval on a mixed-role device does not interrupt unrelated node work. An enqueue invalidated during removal returns a retryable `PAIRING_CHANGED` error instead of claiming success for discarded work. Whitespace-equivalent IDs resolve to the same canonical identity, and existing behavior for ordinary socket disconnects remains unchanged.

Deleting, rotating, or replacing the pairing before first-surface approval also retires that generation-less socket from node lists, environments, active/Talk/remote projections, notifications, inbound RPC, and command-free voice-wake delivery; approval of the unchanged pairing preserves the same identity and only adds surface authority.

If the device key or node token changes while that approval is pending, the approval still succeeds for durable state but does not promote the retired socket or republish its commands, remote caches, or plugin tools; the replacement must authenticate its own transport.

A shared-gateway-auth node whose pairing changes during final connect reconciliation now receives the intended `NOT_PAIRED` rejection instead of hitting an absent device-token authentication binding.

Invalidating a pairing while direct or proxied APNs connection setup is still pending now aborts that setup and directly destroys the active CONNECT request and its socket, so retired ownership cannot leave proxy work alive until the normal timeout.

A later reapproval can no longer make a previously authenticated socket skip directly to that newer generation, and newly paired replacements start with independent wake and nudge state instead of inheriting an older generation's in-flight result or throttle window.

Revoking or replacing a node while one of its asynchronous events is still resolving also prevents that retired connection from sending a receipt or starting an agent turn after the revocation boundary.

If that retired event is a voice transcript, rejecting it no longer consumes the short replay-dedupe window, touches the session store, or registers an orphan chat run, so the same transcript can be accepted immediately from the replacement connection. Racing duplicates for a new session also cannot overwrite the accepted command's generated session ID, commands actually received outside the replay window remain distinct even if slow pairing checks complete together, and a replay revoked while waiting behind an older reservation is rejected before any state or agent work starts.

The same revocation boundary now prevents a partially uploaded Watch result from completing an invocation and prevents stale WebSocket or Watch transports from receiving later voice-wake triggers or routing configuration.

A retired node can no longer refresh the replacement pairing's last-seen timestamp or remain advertised as connected, active, environment-available, or Talk-capable after an external token rotation, revocation, removal, or reapproval. Temporary pairing-store read failures fail closed for capability projection without permanently invalidating a potentially valid session.

If a live node is approved from generation A to B while an older persistent lookup is still pending, that lookup no longer disconnects B. Once a mismatch is independently proven, only the retired connection's active presence and remote node/skill/bin projections are removed; a replacement connection is not erased, and agent prompts omit a stale `active_node` before the model turn starts.

Remote execution hosts and node-hosted skills are no longer advertised indefinitely while the gateway is idle after an out-of-process generation change, and scheduled bin refresh does not probe the retired session. A node removed, reapproved, or silently superseded during the notification delay also produces no false “Node connected” message on another Mac.

A same-ID replacement also starts without the retired node's binary inventory. An older probe that finishes after replacement cannot publish or persist its result, while an ordinary reconnect for the unchanged generation keeps the existing inventory and avoids unnecessary re-probing.

## Evidence

- Prior candidate tree `87766d8` passed controlled formatting, lint, Node 24 EventEmitter contract validation, and source-level invariant checks for the pairing-generation, subscription, queue, transport, and APNs ownership paths. Exact current tree `2841be7` at head `e539350` passes the bound repair-tail `git diff --check` after correcting approval-generation capture, restoring first-surface pending-node compatibility, moving post-handshake connection and presence metadata generation checks into row-scoped SQLite transactions under the shared pairing lock, filtering connected/active/environment projections through loaded durable pairing generations, making Talk and agent active-node selection persistently generation-aware, binding asynchronous connected-session results to their pre-yield object/connection/generation, cleaning remote node/skill/bin projections only for the exact invalidated `connId`, handing the first-connection claim to the current same-generation session after persistence succeeds, owning direct APNs session errors throughout asynchronous currentness validation, resolving rollback-capable voice reservations in receipt order with a final currentness check immediately before committed state and agent startup, and restoring lifecycle cancellation through direct and proxied APNs connection setup. Signal-bearing proxy setup now owns an abortable HTTP CONNECT request, preserves managed HTTPS-proxy CA and authorization handling, explicitly uses the proxy hostname for HTTPS SNI (and disables SNI for IP proxy hosts), and destroys the active request/socket exactly once without adding or moving low-level `http2.connect` boundary calls; the earlier static results are retained only as prior-candidate evidence.
- The controlled current-main-port receipt binds hosted head `4387781`, the initial pinned-main port and exact force-with-lease target. The later sync target binds main `5a6a19c`; the resolved `connect-session.ts` retains both pairing-generation capture and main's authenticated user-profile import, and the current method registry retains the newer talk client methods.
- On the pre-rebase hosted head, a real gateway invocation was held in an in-flight wake while the node was removed, re-paired with the same identity, approved, and connected again. The replacement connected before the old invocation settled but received zero commands from it; both wake-state maps remained absent, the old invocation settled 53 ms after its wake was released, and a fresh disconnected invocation completed in 11 ms without inheriting the three-second delay.
- On that same pre-rebase head, five focused gateway test files passed 94 tests covering both removal APIs, ordinary-disconnect wake preservation, lifecycle release, pending-work propagation, and preventing an invalidated invocation from dispatching to a replacement session. Two additional no-registration leak tests also passed.
- The repair tail adds direct generation-owner coverage; rejects revoked, tokenless, and surface-less admission; proves operator-only approval does not rotate node work while node token/surface changes abort it; binds registered sessions and chat subscriptions to the public key and node token generation used at authentication; blocks retired-generation subscribed events after external reapproval; clears subscription inheritance across replacement while preserving same-generation reconnect and exact live promotion; retires old WebSocket/watch transports after device reapproval; gates every inbound node RPC on persistent generation; transitions the exact connected session on surface reapproval; rereads persistent generation at the centralized dispatch owner; propagates generation through sibling command routes; rejects prior-generation lookup and dispatch without allowing stale work to invalidate the replacement; requires exact current `connId` for destructive drain; validates APNs registration atomically with pairing state; clears shared APNs ownership when the paired device or installation identity is replaced; preserves same-installation and mixed-role operator notification ownership plus replacement registration after commit; rolls back only the exact pending item created by an invalidated enqueue; cancels direct/relay APNs setup at the final write boundary; fixes both generation-bearing pending assertions; and retains the earlier queue, removal, pruning, and APNs race coverage.
- The latest repair keeps current-generation voice-wake updates and delayed connect snapshots on the persistent-generation-aware registry path while preserving command-free delivery to a first-surface pending node. Connect-time pairing state is checked twice; every authenticated session registers with an independent pairing identity, approved sessions also carry their generation, and the exact pending `connId` can transition from no generation to the committed first generation only when the approval transaction, captured session, final durable state, and registry mutation guard all agree on identity. The registry now resolves identity and optional generation together and applies the same state predicate to synchronous and asynchronous connected selection, inventory, environment projection, active/Talk/remote capabilities, inbound RPC, notifications, Watch transport, and delayed command-free snapshots. The repair also fixes test type contracts, restores the APNs HTTP/2 helper to the pinned base so the network-boundary check sees no new low-level connection surface, and resolves review feedback that a retired WebSocket or Watch session could otherwise stamp `lastConnectedAtMs` onto a replacement generation. The final persistence owner reads the current paired row, compares generation, and updates only `node_surface_json` under one immediate SQLite transaction, preventing stale process-local snapshots from restoring retired pairing state. That transaction also participates in the process-local pairing lock, so a node-surface mutation that loaded an earlier full snapshot cannot erase the committed connection timestamp; a deterministic lock-interleaving regression covers this ordering. After the write succeeds, first-connect ownership is resolved through a generation-scoped lookup so a current same-generation reconnect receives the one-time notification while a different pairing replacement is excluded. Direct APNs now installs a consuming session-error owner before the persistent currentness check yields, keeps it until session close, and uses a request-specific listener to reject the active send; a pending-currentness regression emits a connection error and proves no request is written. The regressions reject the retired identity or generation's metadata write, permit the current generation's first-connection claim, preserve that claim across same-generation handoff, block pending identity rotation from promoting the old socket, and prevent external APNs connection failure from becoming an unhandled Gateway error.
- Committed head `a54f38e` (tree `77f676c`) has not yet been run through repository tests, typecheck, full lint, or the real gateway because contributor-controlled repository code is not executed locally in this environment. The controlled repository formatter and real pre-commit hook prepared the 2-file shared-auth failure-owner repair on top of the 6-file approval-transition and 19-file identity/generation candidates; post-commit `git diff --check` and source-level pairing-state invariant validation were sealed against the exact 21-file tree and full submitted diff. Those checks cover the always-present pairing identity used by connect-finalization failure telemetry, absence of the optional authentication-binding dereference, authoritative identity returned from the approval transaction, captured/final identity and generation agreement, exact connection and registry transition guards, stable generation-less promotion for the unchanged pairing, rejection after external node-token rotation, generation-less external deletion, snapshot distinction between a pending surface and a missing pairing row, synchronous and asynchronous identity invalidation, delayed command-free snapshot ownership, identity-aware inventory and environment projection, active/Talk/remote capability selection, inbound RPC, notifications, voice-wake delivery, and Watch transport. The earlier exact-tree checks remain bound to their respective committed candidates and cover transactional presence generation matching, approved-generation projections and dispatch, promotion-race non-invalidation, exact-connection cleanup, APNs cancellation, queue ownership, and fail-closed non-revoking behavior on pairing-store errors. Hosted CI is the remaining exact-head runtime/test validation.
- Committed head `0273bfd` (tree `fe197a6`, effective submitted diff `e0b2b5b`) adds the generation-owned remote-bin repair on top of that reviewed baseline. The exact 9-file candidate passed the repository formatter, real pre-commit hook, controlled owner/invariant validation, and format checking. The checks cover same-generation reconnect preservation, replacement-generation clearing, generation-less hydration refusal, generation-fenced `system.which`/`system.run`, rejection of a probe result after replacement, row-transaction rejection of stale persistence, surface-reapproval clearing, public-key replacement clearing, and node-token rotation clearing. target.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three plugin doctor-contract files read legacy state files during `openclaw doctor` migration with a TOCTOU-prone pattern: `statSync(path)` checks file size, then a separate `await fs.readFile(path)` reads the content. Between the stat and the read, a file could be swapped with a much larger one, bypassing the existing 10 MiB size cap and potentially causing OOM.

Affected files:

1. **Reef** (`extensions/reef/doctor-contract-api.ts`): identity keys and binding registrations
2. **Active Memory** (`extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.ts`): legacy session-toggle JSON
3. **Device Pair** (`extensions/device-pair/doctor-contract-api.ts`): legacy notify state JSON

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor migration runs during `openclaw doctor`, triggered by users to diagnose their installation. The existing 10 MiB safety cap is reasonable for these small JSON legacy blobs, but the stat-then-read pattern has a TOCTOU race: the stat validates one file's size, while the read may consume a different (potentially unbounded) file. Opening the file first and operating on the same descriptor eliminates the race while preserving the existing cap and warning behavior.

## What Changed

All three `readLegacy*FileSafely` helpers now open the descriptor first, validate the size on that descriptor, and read exactly the validated number of bytes:

```typescript
const file = await fs.open(filePath, "r");
try {
  const stat = await file.stat();
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error(`not a regular file: ${filePath}`);
  if (stat.size > MAX_BYTES) {
    throw new Error(`file too large: ${stat.size} bytes exceeds ${MAX_BYTES} bytes: ${filePath}`);
  }
  const size = stat.size;
  const buffer = Buffer.alloc(size);
  let offset = 0;
  while (offset < size) {
    const { bytesRead } = await file.read(buffer, offset, size - offset, offset);
    if (bytesRead === 0) {
      throw new Error(`file shrank during read: ${filePath}`);
    }
    offset += bytesRead;
  }
  return buffer.toString("utf8");
} finally {
  await file.close();
}
```

- `fs.promises.open()` returns a `FileHandle`; `stat()` and the read both operate on the same descriptor, so the inode is pinned after validation.
- The read is bounded to the validated `stat.size`, so a concurrent writer cannot grow the file after the descriptor is opened.
- If the file shrinks after validation, the helper throws instead of silently migrating a partial buffer.
- `try/finally` guarantees `file.close()` even when exceptions are thrown.
- Removed unused `import { statSync }` from all three files.
- The 10 MiB cap and the warning-aware oversized-file path are unchanged from the previous behavior.

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `statSync(path)` → TOCTOU race: file could be swapped before read | Descriptor pins the inode; race impossible |
| Silent partial read if file shrank after stat | Fails closed with a clear error |
| Corrupted oversized file → caught with warning | Caught with warning (unchanged) |
| Valid legacy state under 10 MiB → migrated | Migrated (unchanged) |

## Evidence

### Unit tests

Focused doctor-contract tests pass on the exact PR head, including new oversized-file regression tests for all three plugins:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.test.ts \
  extensions/device-pair/doctor-contract-api.test.ts \
  extensions/reef/doctor-contract-api.test.ts
```

```
 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/0668000387/openclawCxbAsDev/.worktrees/pr110719
 ✓ |extension-active-memory| extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.test.ts (3 tests)
 ✓ |extension-misc| extensions/device-pair/doctor-contract-api.test.ts (3 tests)
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/reef/doctor-contract-api.test.ts (17 tests)
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
 Tests  23 passed (23)
```

### Real `openclaw doctor` runtime proof

A real `openclaw doctor` invocation was run against the PR head with both normal and oversized Active Memory legacy state files.

Normal legacy state (`session-toggles.json` under 10 MiB):

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-doctor-normal-YfRDf9
openclaw doctor
openclaw doctor --fix
```

```
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated 1 Active Memory session toggle entry -> plugin state
- Archived Active Memory session toggles legacy source -> /tmp/oc-doctor-normal-YfRDf9/plugins/active-memory/session-toggles.json.migrated
```

Oversized legacy state (`session-toggles.json` at 10 MiB + 1 byte):

```bash

openclaw doctor
openclaw doctor --fix

```

```
- file too large: 10485761 bytes exceeds 10485760 bytes: /tmp/oc-doctor-oversized-1NEn46/plugins/active-memory/session-toggles.json
```

This confirms the descriptor-bound reader preserves the existing 10 MiB cap: valid files migrate and archive, oversized files are left in place and surfaced as a doctor warning.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(codex): skip runtime setup during CLI metadata registration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the Codex plugin enabled, unknown CLI commands (e.g. `openclaw stats --deep`) previously crashed plugin registration with:

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'openSyncKeyedStore')
```

before the normal unknown-command diagnostic.

This PR partitions `registrationMode` so metadata/setup loads stay side-effect free, **tool-discovery keeps Codex tools/providers**, and full mode retains harness/hooks/commands — matching the plugin SDK contract and ClawSweeper review feedback on #107314.

## Summary

| Mode | Registers |
|---|---|
| `cli-metadata` / `discovery` / `setup-only` / `setup-runtime` | CLI descriptors only |
| `tool-discovery` | tools + media/web-search (+ tool metadata); no harness/hooks/commands |
| `full` | durable runtime (session catalog, harness, migration, commands, hooks) |

Keeps main's lazy binding-store open-on-first-use.

## Evidence (merge-head `8b12f96603`, Node **v24.15.0**)

### Focused tests

```text
pnpm test extensions/codex/index.test.ts extensions/codex/cli-metadata.test.ts
# Tests  28 passed (28)
```

### Mode parity terminal proof (isolated `$OPENCLAW_HOME`, `plugins.entries.codex.enabled=true`)

**1) Unknown command stays clean** (metadata path, no plugin crash):

```text
[openclaw] Reason: Unknown command: openclaw stats. No built-in command or plugin CLI metadata owns "stats".
Did you mean this?
  openclaw status
```

Crash scan for `openSyncKeyedStore` / `TypeError` / `failed during register`: **none**.

**2) `openclaw codex --help` (exit 0):**

```text
Usage: openclaw codex [options] [command]
Inspect and branch from Codex sessions through the Gateway
Commands: archive / continue / help / sessions
```

**3) Live tool/capability discovery — `openclaw plugins inspect codex --runtime --json` (exit 0):**

```text
"id": "codex"
"status": "loaded"
"activated": true
"mediaUnderstandingProviderIds": ["codex"]
"webSearchProviderIds": ["codex"]
"migrationProviderIds": ["codex"]
"cliCommands": ["codex"]
"contracts": {
  "tools": [
    "codex_threads",
    "codex_endpoint_probe",
    ...
  ],
  "mediaUnderstandingProviders": ["codex"],
  "webSearchProviders": ["codex"],
  "migrationProviders": ["codex"]
}
```

**4) Full Gateway activation (foreground `gateway run` on loopback:18799):**

```text
[gateway] loading configuration
[gateway] resolving authentication
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] starting HTTP server...
[health-monitor] started
[plugins] loading ...
[plugins] loaded 13 plugin(s) (13 attempted) in 1055.9ms
TCP 127.0.0.1:18799 OPEN (~45s after start)
No openSyncKeyedStore / TypeError during gateway start.
```

(WS probe budget 3s timed out while plugin sidecars were still settling on a cold Windows start; HTTP listener + plugin load completed without registration crashes.)

### Rebase

Rebased onto current `main` (`83e78d8681` lineage). Conflict resolved: full-mode harness keeps main's `sessionCatalogControl` + `runtime` args.

## Mode × capability matrix

| Surface | metadata/setup | tool-discovery | full |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI descriptors | yes | yes | yes |
| `codex_threads` / media / web-search | no | yes | yes |
| harness / hooks / commands / session catalog | no | no | yes |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests 28/28 on rebased head
- [x] Unknown command clean with codex enabled
- [x] `openclaw codex --help`
- [x] `plugins inspect codex --runtime` shows loaded + contracts.tools (`codex_threads`) + providers
- [x] Gateway starts (HTTP listen + plugin load) without register crash
- [ ] CI green on `8b12f96603`

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

target.title: fix(ollama): release failed setup response bodies before returning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a connection leak where Ollama setup flows (`openclaw configure` / onboarding model pull, cloud auth check, and the tools-capability scan) would leave the HTTP response body unread when a `/api/me`, `/api/pull`, or `/api/show` call returned a non-OK status — or, for `/api/me`, even on success. With a slow or stalled Ollama server (or proxy in front of it), the keep-alive socket stays occupied after the call returns, pinning the connection in the dispatcher pool until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo's established contract for guarded fetches is to cancel the response body before returning on paths that do not consume it (`await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, as in `extensions/huggingface/models.ts` and `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and the merged "cancel redirect relay response body before returning" fix). The SSRF guard's `release()` only closes the dispatcher — it does not drain or cancel an unread response body — so each caller owns this. `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` missed it at four return/throw sites (`/api/me` non-OK and success, `/api/pull` non-OK, `/api/show` non-OK). Each now cancels the body first. Out of scope: other extensions — their error paths already consume the body via `readResponseTextLimited` or cancel it explicitly.

## User Impact

Operators running Ollama setup against a slow, stalled, or misbehaving server no longer leak sockets on failed pulls/auth checks, so repeated setup attempts cannot accumulate pinned keep-alive connections. No behavior change on happy paths beyond releasing the already-unused `/api/me` success body.

## Evidence

Real probe against the production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` with a local keep-alive HTTP stub that answers `HTTP 500` and then holds the response body open forever (slow-peer simulation). The probe counts client sockets still open after the call returns:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # before fix (upstream/main)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:33817
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 368
client sockets still open after return: 1
VERDICT: connection LEAKED — failed response body never released

$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # after fix (this branch)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

Focused suite: new `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` 4/4 pass (all 4 fail against `upstream/main`'s `setup.ts`); full `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` 37/37 pass unchanged; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Ollama setup calls that return non-OK responses (`/api/me`, `/api/pull`, `/api/show`) or a successful `/api/me` leaked the keep-alive connection because the unread response body was never cancelled before returning.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, OpenClaw `main` (7fe1d70a50), production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` from `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` against a real local `node:http` keep-alive server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started a local HTTP stub that returns `HTTP 500` for `/api/me` and streams an unbounded body, called the real `checkOllamaCloudAuth("http://127.0.0.1:<port>")` via `node --import tsx probe.mjs`, then counted client sockets still open one second after the call returned.
- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

- Observed result after fix: the call returns `{ signedIn: false }` as before, but the client socket is released immediately (0 still open, vs 1 leaked before the patch). Regression tests confirm the same for the `/api/pull` and `/api/show` error paths and the `/api/me` success path.
- What was not tested: a live Ollama server (real `ollama pull`); the probe and tests exercise the exact fetch/return paths with real `Response` streams and a real HTTP server.

## Regression test plan

- Target test file: `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` (new companion file; kept out of `setup.test.ts`, which already exceeds the repo's max-lines budget on `main`)
- Scenario locked in: for each fixed path (`/api/me` non-OK, `/api/me` success, `/api/pull` HTTP 500, `/api/show` HTTP 500 during the tools scan), a `Response` whose body stream stays open until cancelled must be cancelled before the function returns or throws.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior changed? No — same return values and error messages; only connection cleanup changes.
- Config/env/migration changed? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No new network surface; failed responses are now released instead of pinned.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Rebased onto origin/main 64c82812a5e. GitHub now reports the PR mergeable; main advanced again after the push, so the exact-merge checks are validating head 6604ba454b7 against the live base.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
